## ARTICLE 1. DEFINITIONS AND RULES OF CONSTRUCTION

### Section 1.1 Definitions.

As used in this Lease, the following capitalized terms have the meanings set forth below. Terms defined elsewhere in this Lease have the meanings there ascribed to them.

"**Abatement Year**" means each successive period of twelve (12) full calendar months commencing on the Abatement Commencement Date, and each anniversary thereof.

"**Abatement Commencement Date**" has the meaning set forth in Section 6.3(a).

"**Affiliate**" means, with respect to any Person: (a) any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with such Person; (b) with respect to Tenant, any entity in which Marcus Ellison holds a direct or indirect controlling interest; (c) Coventry Capital Partners LP and its affiliated funds, general partners, managers, and portfolio companies; (d) any entity resulting from an internal reorganization or restructuring of Tenant's ownership, provided that Marcus Ellison or Coventry Capital Partners LP (or their respective affiliates) retain a controlling interest in the resulting entity; and (e) any investment fund, vehicle, joint venture, or account managed, sponsored, or advised by any of the foregoing or by their respective principals. "Control" means the possession, directly or indirectly, of the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of a Person, whether through the ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise.

"**Applicable Law**" means all present and future statutes, codes, ordinances, regulations, rules, orders, permits, approvals, judgments, and requirements of any Governmental Authority having jurisdiction over the Premises, the Project, or the use or operation thereof, including the ELUR, the Remediation Standard Regulations, the Affordable Housing Covenant, and all zoning, building, coastal, wetlands, floodplain, fire, life-safety, environmental, and accessibility requirements.

"**Approvals**" means all permits, approvals, authorizations, variances, special permits, site plan approvals, coastal and wetlands permits, building permits, certificates of occupancy, and other governmental consents necessary for the development, construction, occupancy, and operation of the Project.

"**Base Rent**" means the annual rent payable under Article 3.

"**Breakpoint**" has the meaning set forth in Section 4.2.

"**Business Day**" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or day on which commercial banks in Connecticut are authorized or required to be closed.

"**CPI**" means the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, Northeast Region, as published by the United States Bureau of Labor Statistics (Series ID CUUR0100SA0), or any successor index designated under Section 3.3(c).

"**Casualty**" means any damage to or destruction of the Premises or the Improvements by fire, flood, windstorm, named storm, storm surge, tidal inundation, earthquake, or other casualty.

"**Condemnation**" means any taking of all or any part of the Premises or the Improvements, or of any interest therein or right appurtenant thereto, by eminent domain, condemnation, inverse condemnation, or conveyance in lieu thereof under threat of the exercise of the power of eminent domain.

"**DEEP**" means the Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection, or any successor agency.

"**ELUR**" means the Environmental Land Use Restriction recorded March 22, 2018, at Volume 412, Page 88 of the Port Calloway Land Records, as the same may be modified, amended, or released from time to time with the approval of DEEP.

"**Environmental Requirements**" means all Applicable Laws relating to pollution, contamination, hazardous substances, petroleum products, soil, sediment, groundwater, surface water, air, wetlands, or the protection of human health or the environment, including the Remediation Standard Regulations (Regs. Conn. State Agencies Section 22a-133k-1 et seq.), the ELUR, and the Connecticut Transfer Act (Section 22a-134 et seq. of the Connecticut General Statutes), together with the terms of any Remedial Action Plan, Soil Management Plan, Environmental Management Plan, or DEEP approval applicable to the Premises.

"**Event of Default**" means a Tenant Event of Default or a Landlord Event of Default, as applicable.

"**Expert**" means an independent third party appointed under Section 18.3(c) to determine any matter designated in this Lease for expert determination.

"**Fair Market Value of the Improvements**" means the fair market value as of the applicable date, determined in accordance with Section 7.7(b), of the Improvements, considered in place, in their then-existing condition, as an undivided whole, excluding Tenant's Trade Fixtures and Personal Property, and determined (i) on the basis of the use permitted under this Lease and the ELUR, (ii) without regard to any encumbrance arising by, through, or under Tenant (other than the Leasehold Mortgage), and (iii) without deduction for the value of Landlord's fee interest in the Land or for the reversion.

"**Force Majeure**" has the meaning set forth in Section 7.4(b).

"**Governmental Authority**" means the United States of America, the State of Connecticut, the City of Port Calloway, Landlord, and any other federal, state, regional, municipal, or local government, agency, board, commission, department, authority, district, or instrumentality having jurisdiction.

"**Gross Revenues**" has the meaning set forth in Section 4.3.

"**Hazardous Materials**" means petroleum and petroleum products, petroleum hydrocarbons, waste oil, diesel, gasoline, volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds, polychlorinated biphenyls, asbestos, lead, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, and any other substance, material, or waste regulated under any Environmental Requirement.

"**Improvements**" means all buildings, structures, foundations, piles, slabs, parking facilities, infrastructure, utility lines within the Premises, hardscape, bulkhead work, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire-protection, and life-safety systems, fixtures, and other improvements, whether above or below grade, now or hereafter constructed, installed, or placed on the Premises by or on behalf of Tenant, together with all alterations, replacements, and additions thereto, but excluding Tenant's Trade Fixtures and Personal Property.

"**Landlord Event of Default**" has the meaning set forth in Section 14.1.

"**Leasehold Mortgage**" means any mortgage, deed of trust, deed to secure debt, collateral assignment of leases and rents, or other security instrument, and any amendment, restatement, renewal, extension, or replacement thereof, encumbering Tenant's leasehold interest in the Premises and the Improvements, granted to a Qualified Mortgagee.

"**Leasehold Mortgagee**" means Bayside and any other Qualified Mortgagee that is the holder, or the designated agent or trustee for the holder(s), of a Leasehold Mortgage, and their respective successors and assigns.

"**Lease Commencement Date**" means the Effective Date, subject to Section 2.6.

"**Lease Year**" — *the parties intend that this term not be used. All references in this Lease are to "Term Year" or "Rent Year," as applicable, as those terms are defined in this Section 1.1 and in Section 2.7.*

"**Memorandum of Lease**" means the memorandum of this Lease in the form of **Exhibit D**, to be recorded in the Port Calloway Land Records.

"**Milestone**" means each of Milestone 1, Milestone 2, Milestone 3, and Milestone 4, as defined in Section 7.3 and scheduled on **Exhibit C**.

"**Milestone Failure**" means Tenant's failure to achieve Milestone 1 or Milestone 3 by the applicable Milestone Deadline, as extended under Section 7.4.

"**Permitted Exceptions**" means the matters listed on **Exhibit I**, as approved by Tenant, and such other matters as Tenant may approve in writing.

"**Person**" means any individual, corporation, limited liability company, partnership, joint venture, trust, estate, association, Governmental Authority, or other entity.

"**Personal Property**" means Tenant's furniture, furnishings, equipment, inventory, computer and communications systems, art, and other personal property that is not a fixture.

"**Project**" has the meaning set forth in Recital C, as further described in Article 9.

"**Qualified Mortgagee**" means (a) Bayside Federal Lending Corp.; (b) any bank, savings bank, savings and loan association, credit union, insurance company, pension fund, real estate investment trust, mortgage real estate investment trust, governmental or quasi-governmental lender, or other institutional lender or financial institution; (c) any trust, fund, or vehicle sponsored, managed, or advised by any of the foregoing; and (d) any other Person approved in writing by Landlord, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, and which approval shall not be required for any assignment or transfer by a Qualified Mortgagee to its Affiliate, to any participant or co-lender, or to any Person acquiring the Leasehold Mortgage upon foreclosure or by deed in lieu.

"**Remediation**" means the investigation, removal, excavation, transportation, disposal, treatment, capping, monitoring, and other remedial activities necessary to address the Contamination in accordance with the Remediation Standard Regulations, the ELUR, and the Remedial Action Plan.

"**Remediation Credit**" has the meaning set forth in Section 5.3(a).

"**Remediation Costs**" means all costs of performing the Remediation, including excavation, transportation, disposal, backfill, confirmation sampling, oversight, reporting, DEEP fees, LEP fees, and permitting, together with the cost of the Soil Management Plan, the Remedial Action Plan, the verification report, and any ELUR modification obtained at Tenant's request.

"**Rent Commencement Date**" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.7.

"**Rent Year**" means (a) the period commencing on the Rent Commencement Date and ending on the day preceding the first anniversary of the Rent Commencement Date, and (b) each successive period of twelve (12) full calendar months thereafter during the Term.

"**Security Deposit**" has the meaning set forth in Section 8.1.

"**Subsidy**" — *not applicable. No rental subsidy, operating subsidy, or public housing assistance is assumed in this Lease, and none shall be imputed to Gross Revenues or to Affordable Units.*

"**Tenant Event of Default**" has the meaning set forth in Section 15.1.

"**Term**" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.5.

"**Term Year**" means (a) the period commencing on the Lease Commencement Date and ending on the day preceding the first anniversary of the Lease Commencement Date, and (b) each successive period of twelve (12) full calendar months thereafter during the Term.

"**Trade Fixtures**" means Tenant's trade fixtures, machinery, equipment, and personal property that are customarily removable without structural damage, including restaurant, retail, fitness, and office equipment and systems, and including all items installed by or for subtenants.

"**Transfer**" means any assignment, sublease of the entire Premises or substantially all of the Premises, conveyance, sale, transfer, or other disposition of this Lease or of Tenant's leasehold interest, whether voluntary, involuntary, direct, or indirect, by operation of law or otherwise.

### Section 1.2 Rules of Construction.

(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation. (b) "Including" means "including without limitation." (c) "Hereof," "herein," "hereunder," and similar terms refer to this Lease as a whole. (d) References to Articles, Sections, and Exhibits are to this Lease. (e) The singular includes the plural and vice versa, and any gender includes all genders. (f) "Days" means calendar days unless Business Days are specified. (g) References to any statute, regulation, or instrument include amendments, replacements, and successors. (h) References to "written" or "in writing" include electronic transmission. (i) Amounts of money are in United States dollars. (j) Where a period is measured from a date, the day of the triggering event is excluded and the last day is included. (k) If any date falls on a day that is not a Business Day, the date shall be the next Business Day. (l) Any determination of "reasonable" satisfaction, consent, or approval shall be made in good faith, in accordance with objective commercial standards, and within the time periods specified in this Lease.

### Section 1.3 Exhibits.

The following Exhibits are incorporated in and made a part of this Lease:

| Exhibit | Description |
|---|---|
| A | Legal Description of the Premises |
| B | Base Rent Schedule and Percentage Rent Illustration |
| C | Development Milestone Schedule |
| D | Form of Memorandum of Lease |
| E | Form of Subordination, Non-Disturbance, and Attornment Agreement |
| F | Form of Letter of Credit |
| G | Affordable Housing Requirements |
| H | Remediation Scope, Cost Allocation, and Credit Schedule |
| I | Permitted Exceptions |

### Section 1.4 No Strict Construction.

This Lease is the product of negotiation between sophisticated parties, each represented by counsel. No provision shall be construed against either party as the drafter. The Term Sheet is superseded in its entirety by this Lease as provided in Section 18.11, and in the event of any conflict between this Lease and the Term Sheet, this Lease controls.

## ARTICLE 2. PREMISES; TERM; APPURTENANCES

### Section 2.1 Demise.

Landlord hereby leases the Premises to Tenant, and Tenant hereby leases the Premises from Landlord, for the Term, subject to the terms, covenants, and conditions of this Lease and the Permitted Exceptions. Tenant's interest is a leasehold estate for years and is not a tenancy at will, tenancy from year to year, or estate in fee.

### Section 2.2 Legal Description; Survey.

(a) The Premises are more particularly described on **Exhibit A**, which shall consist of the metes and bounds description and the certified ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey prepared by Calloway Land Surveyors LLC bearing Survey Job No. CLS-2025-0417, dated April 28, 2025 (the "Survey"), certified to Landlord, Tenant, Ridgepoint Title & Escrow Co., and Bayside.

(b) Landlord and Tenant acknowledge that two legal descriptions of the Premises are in circulation in the transaction record: (i) the description derived from the Survey, describing a parcel with approximately 435.22 feet of frontage on Pier Street and approximately 320.47 feet of frontage on Harbor Avenue, containing 139,392 square feet; and (ii) the description attached as Exhibit A to Title Commitment No. TC-2025-07821 issued by Ridgepoint Title & Escrow Co., which describes courses of 580.00 feet and 480.00 feet and which, when computed, encloses approximately 279,535 square feet (6.42 acres). The parties agree that the description derived from the Survey governs, that the description in the Title Commitment is erroneous, and that **Exhibit A** shall consist exclusively of the Survey description. Landlord shall cause the title company to amend Title Commitment No. TC-2025-07821 accordingly, and the issuance of the leasehold title policies described in Section 17.1(f) reflecting the corrected description is a condition to the Lease Commencement Date under Section 2.6. The stated area of 139,392 square feet is controlling for all purposes of this Lease, including the calculation of rent per square foot, notwithstanding any variance disclosed by field computation or later survey.

(c) Promptly following the Effective Date, and in any event before submission of the first building permit application, the parties shall jointly cause a boundary survey update to reconcile the linear-footage references in the transaction record, including the statement in the Term Sheet, the Title Commitment, the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment, and the Survey narrative that the Premises include "approximately 480 linear feet of bulkhead frontage," against the 320.47-foot eastern boundary shown in the Survey. The cost of such update shall be borne one-half by each party, and neither party shall be in default by reason of any inconsistency described in this Section 2.2 pending completion of the update.

### Section 2.3 Appurtenant Rights.

Tenant's leasehold estate includes, without additional rent: (a) the right to use, maintain, repair, replace, and reconstruct the bulkhead and all waterfront improvements within the Premises; (b) all easements, rights-of-way, and appurtenances benefiting the Premises; (c) the right of ingress and egress over Pier Street, Harbor Avenue, and the public pedestrian promenade; (d) the right to install, maintain, and connect to utilities; and (e) the right to use the air space above the Premises in accordance with Applicable Law, subject to all height, zoning, and Federal Aviation Administration limitations.

### Section 2.4 Reservations; Public Rights.

(a) Landlord reserves no rights in the Premises except: (i) the rights of the public under the recorded public utility easement (Volume 388, Page 201) and the recorded public pedestrian access easement (Volume 395, Page 112), both of which are Permitted Exceptions; (ii) the right to inspect and to exercise its rights under this Lease; and (iii) the reversion at the expiration or earlier termination of the Term.

(b) Landlord shall not grant, and shall not suffer to exist, any easement, license, lease, or other interest in the Premises that would materially and adversely interfere with Tenant's development or operation of the Project, and any such grant without Tenant's prior written consent shall be void as against Tenant's leasehold interest.

(c) Landlord shall use reasonable efforts, at Tenant's request and at Tenant's cost (except as provided in Section 5.5), to relocate, modify, or subordinate any utility facilities within the public utility easement that conflict with the Project, and shall cooperate with Tenant in obtaining any required relocation agreement from the City of Port Calloway.

### Section 2.5 Term.

The term of this Lease (the "Term") is ninety-nine (99) years, commencing on the Lease Commencement Date and expiring at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on September 30, 2124 (the "Expiration Date"), unless sooner terminated as provided in this Lease. No renewal option is granted; the ninety-nine (99) year Term is the full duration of this Lease.

### Section 2.6 Lease Commencement; Conditions Precedent.

(a) The Lease Commencement Date shall be the Effective Date; provided that if any of the following conditions has not been satisfied (or waived in writing by the party entitled to the benefit thereof) on or before the Effective Date, the Lease Commencement Date shall be the date on which the last such condition is satisfied:

> (i) execution and delivery of this Lease, the Memorandum of Lease, and the SNDA;
>
> (ii) delivery by Ridgepoint Title & Escrow Co. of a pro forma ALTA Leasehold Owner's Policy in the amount of $425,000,000 and an ALTA Leasehold Loan Policy in the amount of $285,000,000, in each case in the forms and with the endorsements described in Section 17.1(f), subject only to the Permitted Exceptions;
>
> (iii) delivery of the certified ALTA/NSPS Survey described in Section 2.2(a), together with the corrected legal description described in Section 2.2(b);
>
> (iv) delivery of the Security Deposit in accordance with Article 8;
>
> (v) discharge, bonding, or other disposition of the mechanics' lien filed by Calloway Marine Demolition Inc. on April 3, 2025, in the manner contemplated by Section 17.1(g), so that such lien is not a Permitted Exception and does not appear as an exception to either leasehold policy;
>
> (vi) delivery of evidence of Landlord's authority to execute this Lease, including a certified copy of Resolution No. 2025-047 bearing the vote of the Board of Commissioners and the Chair's certification, together with such additional approvals of the City of Port Calloway as may be required by Section 17.1(b);
>
> (vii) execution and delivery by the City of Port Calloway and Tenant of the Tax Abatement Agreement described in Section 6.3(b); and
>
> (viii) receipt by Tenant of confirmation from DEEP, in form reasonably satisfactory to Tenant, that the ground-floor uses contemplated by the Project as described in Section 9.3 (including residential lobby, leasing office, package room, resident lounge, and fitness center) do not constitute "residential use" prohibited by the ELUR, or, alternatively, Tenant's receipt of a modification of the ELUR permitting the same.

(b) If any condition in Section 2.6(a) has not been satisfied on or before March 31, 2026 (as such date may be extended by mutual written agreement), either party may terminate this Lease by written notice, whereupon the Security Deposit shall be returned to Tenant, neither party shall have any further obligation except for those that expressly survive, and Landlord shall reimburse Tenant for Tenant's documented third-party due diligence costs (including title, survey, environmental, and legal fees incurred with respect to this Lease) up to a maximum aggregate amount of $750,000, but only if the unsatisfied condition is one that Landlord is obligated to satisfy under this Lease.

### Section 2.7 Rent Commencement Date.

The "Rent Commencement Date" is the earlier of: (a) the date that is thirty-six (36) months after the Lease Commencement Date; or (b) the date on which a temporary or permanent certificate of occupancy is issued for Occupancy Trigger Space. "**Occupancy Trigger Space**" means (i) not less than seventy-five percent (75%) of the residential dwelling units included in the Residential Tower, measured by unit count, together with (ii) the ground-floor retail space, such that the Project is ready for occupancy in a manner consistent with the Project's leasing program; provided that if certificates of occupancy are issued for portions of the Project from time to time, Base Rent shall not commence until the Occupancy Trigger Space threshold is met, and no certificate of occupancy for a nominal, incidental, or partial portion of the Project (including a sales center, leasing office, model unit, or stand-alone retail bay) shall accelerate the Rent Commencement Date. From the Lease Commencement Date through the day preceding the Rent Commencement Date (the "Rent Abatement Period"), no Base Rent or Percentage Rent shall be payable, but Tenant shall pay all real property taxes (as abated under Article 6), insurance premiums, utilities, and other operating costs of the Premises.

## ARTICLE 2. PREMISES; TERM; APPURTENANCES

### Section 2.1 Demise.

Landlord hereby leases the Premises to Tenant, and Tenant hereby leases the Premises from Landlord, for the Term, subject to the terms, covenants, and conditions of this Lease and the Permitted Exceptions. Tenant's interest is a leasehold estate for years and is not a tenancy at will, tenancy from year to year, or estate in fee.

### Section 2.2 Legal Description; Survey.

(a) The Premises are more particularly described on **Exhibit A**, which shall consist of the metes and bounds description and the certified ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey prepared by Calloway Land Surveyors LLC bearing Survey Job No. CLS-2025-0417, dated April 28, 2025 (the "Survey"), certified to Landlord, Tenant, Ridgepoint Title & Escrow Co., and Bayside.

(b) Landlord and Tenant acknowledge that two legal descriptions of the Premises are in circulation in the transaction record: (i) the description derived from the Survey, describing a parcel with approximately 435.22 feet of frontage on Pier Street and approximately 320.47 feet of frontage on Harbor Avenue, containing 139,392 square feet; and (ii) the description attached as Exhibit A to Title Commitment No. TC-2025-07821 issued by Ridgepoint Title & Escrow Co., which describes courses of 580.00 feet and 480.00 feet and which, when computed, encloses approximately 279,535 square feet (6.42 acres). The parties agree that the description derived from the Survey governs, that the description in the Title Commitment is erroneous, and that **Exhibit A** shall consist exclusively of the Survey description. Landlord shall cause the title company to amend Title Commitment No. TC-2025-07821 accordingly, and the issuance of the leasehold title policies described in Section 17.1(f) reflecting the corrected description is a condition to the Lease Commencement Date under Section 2.6. The stated area of 139,392 square feet is controlling for all purposes of this Lease, including the calculation of rent per square foot, notwithstanding any variance disclosed by field computation or later survey.

(c) Promptly following the Effective Date, and in any event before submission of the first building permit application, the parties shall jointly cause a boundary survey update to reconcile the linear-footage references in the transaction record, including the statement in the Term Sheet, the Title Commitment, the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment, and the Survey narrative that the Premises include "approximately 480 linear feet of bulkhead frontage," against the 320.47-foot eastern boundary shown in the Survey. The cost of such update shall be borne one-half by each party, and neither party shall be in default by reason of any inconsistency described in this Section 2.2 pending completion of the update.

### Section 2.3 Appurtenant Rights.

Tenant's leasehold estate includes, without additional rent: (a) the right to use, maintain, repair, replace, and reconstruct the bulkhead and all waterfront improvements within the Premises; (b) all easements, rights-of-way, and appurtenances benefiting the Premises; (c) the right of ingress and egress over Pier Street, Harbor Avenue, and the public pedestrian promenade; (d) the right to install, maintain, and connect to utilities; and (e) the right to use the air space above the Premises in accordance with Applicable Law, subject to all height, zoning, and Federal Aviation Administration limitations.

### Section 2.4 Reservations; Public Rights.

(a) Landlord reserves no rights in the Premises except: (i) the rights of the public under the recorded public utility easement (Volume 388, Page 201) and the recorded public pedestrian access easement (Volume 395, Page 112), both of which are Permitted Exceptions; (ii) the right to inspect and to exercise its rights under this Lease; and (iii) the reversion at the expiration or earlier termination of the Term.

(b) Landlord shall not grant, and shall not suffer to exist, any easement, license, lease, or other interest in the Premises that would materially and adversely interfere with Tenant's development or operation of the Project, and any such grant without Tenant's prior written consent shall be void as against Tenant's leasehold interest.

(c) Landlord shall use reasonable efforts, at Tenant's request and at Tenant's cost (except as provided in Section 5.5), to relocate, modify, or subordinate any utility facilities within the public utility easement that conflict with the Project, and shall cooperate with Tenant in obtaining any required relocation agreement from the City of Port Calloway.

### Section 2.5 Term.

The term of this Lease (the "Term") is ninety-nine (99) years, commencing on the Lease Commencement Date and expiring at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on September 30, 2124 (the "Expiration Date"), unless sooner terminated as provided in this Lease. No renewal option is granted; the ninety-nine (99) year Term is the full duration of this Lease.

### Section 2.6 Lease Commencement; Conditions Precedent.

(a) The Lease Commencement Date shall be the Effective Date; provided that if any of the following conditions has not been satisfied (or waived in writing by the party entitled to the benefit thereof) on or before the Effective Date, the Lease Commencement Date shall be the date on which the last such condition is satisfied:

> (i) execution and delivery of this Lease, the Memorandum of Lease, and the SNDA;
>
> (ii) delivery by Ridgepoint Title & Escrow Co. of a pro forma ALTA Leasehold Owner's Policy in the amount of $425,000,000 and an ALTA Leasehold Loan Policy in the amount of $285,000,000, in each case in the forms and with the endorsements described in Section 17.1(f), subject only to the Permitted Exceptions;
>
> (iii) delivery of the certified ALTA/NSPS Survey described in Section 2.2(a), together with the corrected legal description described in Section 2.2(b);
>
> (iv) delivery of the Security Deposit in accordance with Article 8;
>
> (v) discharge, bonding, or other disposition of the mechanics' lien filed by Calloway Marine Demolition Inc. on April 3, 2025, in the manner contemplated by Section 17.1(g), so that such lien is not a Permitted Exception and does not appear as an exception to either leasehold policy;
>
> (vi) delivery of evidence of Landlord's authority to execute this Lease, including a certified copy of Resolution No. 2025-047 bearing the vote of the Board of Commissioners and the Chair's certification, together with such additional approvals of the City of Port Calloway as may be required by Section 17.1(b);
>
> (vii) execution and delivery by the City of Port Calloway and Tenant of the Tax Abatement Agreement described in Section 6.3(b); and
>
> (viii) receipt by Tenant of confirmation from DEEP, in form reasonably satisfactory to Tenant, that the ground-floor uses contemplated by the Project as described in Section 9.3 (including residential lobby, leasing office, package room, resident lounge, and fitness center) do not constitute "residential use" prohibited by the ELUR, or, alternatively, Tenant's receipt of a modification of the ELUR permitting the same.

(b) If any condition in Section 2.6(a) has not been satisfied on or before March 31, 2026 (as such date may be extended by mutual written agreement), either party may terminate this Lease by written notice, whereupon the Security Deposit shall be returned to Tenant, neither party shall have any further obligation except for those that expressly survive, and Landlord shall reimburse Tenant for Tenant's documented third-party due diligence costs (including title, survey, environmental, and legal fees incurred with respect to this Lease) up to a maximum aggregate amount of $750,000, but only if the unsatisfied condition is one that Landlord is obligated to satisfy under this Lease.

### Section 2.7 Rent Commencement Date.

The "Rent Commencement Date" is the earlier of: (a) the date that is thirty-six (36) months after the Lease Commencement Date; or (b) the date on which a temporary or permanent certificate of occupancy is issued for Occupancy Trigger Space. "**Occupancy Trigger Space**" means (i) not less than seventy-five percent (75%) of the residential dwelling units included in the Residential Tower, measured by unit count, together with (ii) the ground-floor retail space, such that the Project is ready for occupancy in a manner consistent with the Project's leasing program; provided that if certificates of occupancy are issued for portions of the Project from time to time, Base Rent shall not commence until the Occupancy Trigger Space threshold is met, and no certificate of occupancy for a nominal, incidental, or partial portion of the Project (including a sales center, leasing office, model unit, or stand-alone retail bay) shall accelerate the Rent Commencement Date. From the Lease Commencement Date through the day preceding the Rent Commencement Date (the "Rent Abatement Period"), no Base Rent or Percentage Rent shall be payable, but Tenant shall pay all real property taxes (as abated under Article 6), insurance premiums, utilities, and other operating costs of the Premises.

### Section 2.8 Memorandum of Lease; Recording.

(a) Concurrently with the execution of this Lease, the parties shall execute, acknowledge, and deliver the Memorandum of Lease in the form of **Exhibit D**, and Tenant shall record the Memorandum of Lease in the Port Calloway Land Records at Tenant's cost. The Memorandum of Lease shall state the identity of the parties, the legal description of the Premises, the Term, the Renewal Prohibition (if any), the Leasehold Mortgage consent, the new lease and cure rights under Article 10, and such other matters as either party may reasonably require.

(b) Recording of the Memorandum of Lease shall not create any obligation of confidentiality as to terms that are required to be disclosed under the Connecticut Freedom of Information Act (Section 1-200 et seq. of the Connecticut General Statutes), and Landlord's disclosure obligations under that Act are governed by Section 18.7.

(c) Neither party shall record this Lease in its entirety without the other party's written consent, except as required by Applicable Law, by a Leasehold Mortgagee, or by the title company as a condition to issuance of the leasehold policies.

### Section 2.9 Condition of the Premises; Delivery.

Tenant accepts the Premises in their present "AS IS, WHERE IS" condition, subject to: (a) Landlord's representations and warranties in Section 17.1; (b) Landlord's covenants in Article 5; and (c) the environmental disclosures in the Phase I Environmental Site Assessment dated March 15, 2025 (Halcyon Project No. HEC-2025-0318) and the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment dated May 2, 2025 (Halcyon Project No. HEC-2025-0412). Landlord shall deliver exclusive possession of the Premises on the Lease Commencement Date, free of all tenants, occupants, and parties in possession other than the holders of the Permitted Exceptions, and free of any lease, license, or option (other than the recorded right of first refusal described on **Exhibit I**).

### Section 2.10 Adjoining Parcel.

Landlord owns Assessor's Parcel No. 127-003-0044, adjoining the Premises to the south and identified for future public park development. Landlord shall: (a) not use or develop such parcel in a manner that unreasonably interferes with the construction, use, operation, or value of the Project, including by way of noise, dust, vibration, staging, or obstruction of light and air; (b) coordinate any construction on such parcel with Tenant's construction schedule; and (c) grant Tenant a temporary construction license over such parcel, at Tenant's cost and insurable by Tenant, for crane and equipment swing, staging, and access during the construction period, on reasonable terms to be documented before commencement of construction.

## ARTICLE 3. BASE RENT

### Section 3.1 Initial Base Rent.

Commencing on the Rent Commencement Date, Tenant shall pay initial annual Base Rent of **Two Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars ($2,850,000)** (approximately $20.45 per square foot per annum based on 139,392 square feet), payable in equal monthly installments of Two Hundred Thirty-Seven Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($237,500) on or before the first day of each calendar month, without notice or demand.

### Section 3.2 Fixed Escalation (Rent Years 1 through 15).

Base Rent shall escalate by two and one-half percent (2.5%) per annum, compounded annually, applied in five (5) year steps from the initial Base Rent, so that annual Base Rent is as follows:

| Rent Years | Annual Base Rent | Monthly Installment (annual amount / 12) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 through 5 | $2,850,000 | $237,500.00 |
| 6 through 10 | $3,224,513 | $268,709.42 |
| 11 through 15 | $3,648,241 | $304,020.08 |

The amounts in the table are computed as $2,850,000 multiplied by 1.025 raised to the fifth and tenth powers, respectively, and rounded to the nearest whole dollar. If any amount stated in the table differs from the amount produced by that formula, the formula controls, and the monthly installment shall in all events equal one-twelfth of the annual amount determined under the formula, rounded to the nearest cent. The schedule of Base Rent for the full Term appears on **Exhibit B**.

### Section 3.3 CPI Reset (Rent Year 16 and Thereafter).

(a) Effective on the first day of Rent Year 16 and on the first day of each tenth (10th) Rent Year thereafter (that is, Rent Years 26, 36, 46, 56, 66, 76, 86, and 96) (each, a "**Reset Date**"), annual Base Rent shall be reset to the greater of:

> (i) the amount that would result from the continued application of the two and one-half percent (2.5%) per annum compounding escalation set forth in Section 3.2 from the initial Base Rent of $2,850,000, determined as of such Reset Date; and
>
> (ii) the initial Base Rent of $2,850,000, multiplied by a fraction, the numerator of which is the CPI for the calendar month that is three (3) months before the applicable Reset Date and the denominator of which is the CPI for the calendar month that is three (3) months before the Lease Commencement Date (the "Base Index Month").

(b) In no event shall any reset under clause (ii) exceed, in the aggregate, one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the increase that would result under clause (i) as of the same Reset Date (the "Reset Cap"). Base Rent shall not be reduced at any Reset Date below the amount payable immediately before such Reset Date.

(c) If the CPI ceases to be published, the parties shall use the most comparable index published by the United States Bureau of Labor Statistics or, if none, a successor index designated by the Expert under Section 18.3(c), rebased to the Base Index Month.

(d) Each reset shall be binding on the parties when determined. Either party may, within thirty (30) days after receipt of the other party's calculation, object in writing, in which case the matter shall be determined by an Expert under Section 18.3(c), whose fees shall be borne equally. Pending determination, Tenant shall pay Base Rent at the amount calculated by Tenant, subject to reconciliation with interest at the lesser of eight percent (8%) per annum and the maximum lawful rate.

### Section 3.4 Payment; Application.

(a) Base Rent and Percentage Rent shall be paid in lawful money of the United States by electronic funds transfer or other method reasonably designated by Landlord, without prior demand.

(b) Rent paid shall be applied first to Base Rent then due, then to Percentage Rent then due, then to any other amounts then due under this Lease. No payment shall be deemed a waiver of any right, and no acceptance of a partial payment shall constitute an accord and satisfaction.

(c) Tenant shall deliver to Landlord an annual rent statement within thirty (30) days after the end of each Rent Year, showing Base Rent, Percentage Rent, all offsets and credits applied, and the then-current Base Rent and Breakpoint for the following Rent Year. Administrative error in a statement shall not affect the obligations of the parties, which shall be reconciled within thirty (30) days after discovery.

### Section 3.5 Setoff.

Tenant's obligation to pay rent is absolute and unconditional, except that Tenant may offset against Base Rent, upon ten (10) Business Days' prior written notice and in accordance with the procedures of this Lease: (a) the Remediation Credit under Section 5.3; (b) any amount due from Landlord under Section 6.4 as a result of the failure or shortfall of the tax abatement; (c) any amount due from Landlord under Section 14.4 following a Landlord Event of Default; (d) any amount due from Landlord under Section 7.7 upon a Reverter Termination; (e) any refund of an overpayment of Percentage Rent under Section 4.7; and (f) any amount finally determined to be due from Landlord to Tenant under this Lease, including under Article 13. Amounts not disputed in good faith may be offset without further condition. Landlord's acceptance of reduced rent under this Section shall not constitute a waiver of any claim.

### Section 3.6 Late Payment.

Any installment of rent not received within five (5) Business Days after its due date shall bear interest from the due date at the lesser of (a) eight percent (8%) per annum and (b) the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law. Landlord may impose a late charge of three percent (3%) of the overdue installment, provided that Landlord shall not impose more than two (2) late charges in any twelve (12) month period, and no late charge or interest shall accrue on amounts properly withheld or offset under Section 3.5 or disputed in good faith under this Lease.

### Section 3.7 Proration.

Rent for any partial calendar month shall be prorated on a per diem basis based on the actual number of days in the month. Rent for any partial Rent Year shall be prorated on a per diem basis based on a 365-day year.

### Section 3.8 Rent Absolute.

Except as expressly provided in this Lease, rent is not subject to any abatement, deduction, counterclaim, or setoff arising from any cause, including any defect in the Premises, any failure of Landlord to perform, any interruption of the Project's business, or any Casualty or Condemnation except as provided in Article 13. Tenant waives, to the fullest extent permitted by Applicable Law, any right to terminate this Lease or to withhold rent by reason of any such cause, except as expressly set forth in this Lease; provided that nothing in this Section limits Tenant's rights under Article 10, Article 13, or Article 14, or Tenant's rights against the Leasehold Mortgagee, or any non-waivable statutory right under the laws of the State of Connecticut.

## ARTICLE 4. PERCENTAGE RENT

### Section 4.1 Obligation.

Commencing with Rent Year 6 and continuing for the remainder of the Term, Tenant shall pay to Landlord, as additional rent, Percentage Rent equal to two percent (2.0%) of the amount by which Gross Revenues for such Rent Year exceed the Breakpoint for such Rent Year.

### Section 4.2 Breakpoint; Breakpoint Adjustment.

(a) The Breakpoint for Rent Year 6 is **Twenty-Eight Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($28,500,000)**.

(b) The Breakpoint is not a permanently fixed amount. Effective on the first day of each Rent Year after Rent Year 5, the Breakpoint shall be increased by the same cumulative percentage by which Base Rent has increased from Rent Year 1 to such Rent Year, determined under Sections 3.2 and 3.3, so that the ratio of the Breakpoint to Base Rent remains constant at ten to one (10.0x) throughout the Term. The Breakpoint shall never be reduced below $28,500,000.

(c) On or before the first day of Rent Year 6, and on or before the first day of each Rent Year thereafter, Landlord and Tenant shall confirm in writing the Breakpoint for such Rent Year. Either party may request an Expert determination of the Breakpoint under Section 18.3(c); pending determination, Percentage Rent shall be paid on the basis of the Breakpoint calculated by Tenant, subject to reconciliation.

(d) The parties acknowledge that Percentage Rent is intended to be a participation in the upside of the Project above the level of performance projected by the parties in 2025, and is not intended to operate as a gross receipts tax that increases in real terms over the Term solely because of inflation. The adjustment mechanism in this Section 4.2 is intended to give effect to that intent, and shall govern the construction of this Article 4.

### Section 4.3 Gross Revenues.

"**Gross Revenues**" means, for any Rent Year, the gross revenues actually received in cash by Tenant and its Affiliates from the operation of the Project during such Rent Year, determined on a cash receipts basis (and not on the accrual or straight-line basis), consisting of: (a) residential rents (including rent for Affordable Units), net of concessions, abatements, and free rent actually granted; (b) office rents and additional rent actually received; (c) retail rents and additional rent actually received; (d) parking revenues; and (e) ancillary income directly derived from the operation of the Project, including fees for amenities actually paid by residents and commercial tenants.

### Section 4.4 Exclusions from Gross Revenues.

Gross Revenues shall exclude: (a) security deposits, except to the extent actually applied by Tenant to rent in default and then only in the Rent Year so applied; (b) utility charges and reimbursements; (c) common area maintenance, real estate tax, insurance, and other operating expense recoveries and pass-throughs, including any recovery from subtenants or occupants of a proportionate share of costs; (d) proceeds of insurance; (e) condemnation awards and sale or refinancing proceeds; (f) interest, dividends, and other investment income; (g) capital contributions, loans, or other financing proceeds; (h) tenant improvement allowances, construction management fees, development fees, and other charges paid by subtenants or occupants in connection with fitting out space, to the extent they reimburse Tenant's capital costs; (i) reimbursements of Remediation Costs or of the cost of the engineered barrier; (j) any payment, credit, or refund received from Landlord or any Governmental Authority, including under the Tax Abatement Agreement; (k) rent attributable to Tenant's own use space, and rent from any subtenant that is an Affiliate to the extent it exceeds arm's-length rent; (l) recoveries of amounts previously written off; (m) revenue attributable to the public open space described in Section 9.5; (n) rebates, discounts, and vendor refunds; (o) proceeds from the sale of assets, furniture, fixtures, and equipment; (p) late fees, interest, and default interest; and (q) any amounts received in respect of periods before the Rent Commencement Date.

### Section 4.5 Statements; Payment.

Percentage Rent shall be calculated annually and shall be due within ninety (90) days after the end of each Rent Year, accompanied by a certified statement of Gross Revenues for such Rent Year, prepared on a cash basis consistent with this Article 4, and signed by an authorized financial officer of Tenant. Tenant shall maintain complete and accurate books and records supporting Gross Revenues for not less than three (3) years after the end of each Rent Year.

### Section 4.6 Audit.

(a) Landlord may, no more than once in any Rent Year, at its sole cost, audit Tenant's books and records relating to Gross Revenues for the two (2) most recently completed Rent Years, upon not less than forty-five (45) days' prior written notice, during regular business hours, at the office where such records are maintained, through an independent certified public accountant bound by confidentiality obligations reasonably acceptable to Tenant and compensated on an hourly basis (and not on a contingency or percentage basis).

(b) Tenant shall have no obligation to produce records for any Rent Year more than twenty-four (24) months after delivery of the statement for that Rent Year, and Landlord's failure to object to a statement within such period shall be deemed acceptance of the statement for that Rent Year.

(c) If an audit demonstrates that Tenant underpaid Percentage Rent by five percent (5%) or more for the audited Rent Year, Tenant shall reimburse Landlord's reasonable, documented audit costs. If the audit demonstrates an underpayment of less than five percent (5%), or an overpayment, Landlord shall bear its own audit costs.

### Section 4.7 Overpayment and Underpayment.

(a) Any underpayment established by an audit or by mutual agreement shall be paid within thirty (30) days after final determination, together with interest at the rate in Section 3.6 from the original due date.

(b) Any overpayment shall, at Tenant's election, be credited against the next installments of Percentage Rent or Base Rent, or refunded within thirty (30) days, together with interest at the rate in Section 3.6.

(c) The obligations of this Section 4.7 survive the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease for a period of two (2) years.

### Section 4.8 Confidentiality of Revenue Data.

Landlord shall treat all statements of Gross Revenues and audit results as confidential, and shall disclose them only to its officers, commissioners, attorneys, auditors, and financial advisors, or as required by the Connecticut Freedom of Information Act or other Applicable Law, and shall assert all available exemptions before disclosure.

| Rent Years | Annual Base Rent | Monthly Installment (annual amount / 12) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 through 5 | $2,850,000 | $237,500.00 |
| 6 through 10 | $3,224,513 | $268,709.42 |
| 11 through 15 | $3,648,241 | $304,020.08 |

The amounts in the table are computed as $2,850,000 multiplied by 1.025 raised to the fifth and tenth powers, respectively, and rounded to the nearest whole dollar. Amounts not disputed in good faith may be offset without further condition. Landlord's acceptance of reduced rent under this Section shall not constitute a waiver of any claim.

### Section 3.6 Late Payment.

Any installment of rent not received within five (5) Business Days after its due date shall bear interest from the due date at the lesser of (a) eight percent (8%) per annum and (b) the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law. Landlord may impose a late charge of three percent (3%) of the overdue installment, provided that Landlord shall not impose more than two (2) late charges in any twelve (12) month period, and no late charge or interest shall accrue on amounts properly withheld or offset under Section 3.5 or disputed in good faith under this Lease.

### Section 3.7 Proration.

Except as expressly provided in this Lease, rent is not subject to any abatement, deduction, counterclaim, or setoff arising from any cause, including any defect in the Premises, any failure of Landlord to perform, any interruption of the Project's business, or any Casualty or Condemnation except as provided in Article 13. ## ARTICLE 5. ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS; REMEDIATION

### Section 5.1 Landlord's Environmental Representations.

Landlord represents and warrants to Tenant that, as of the Effective Date and as of the Lease Commencement Date:

(a) The Phase I Environmental Site Assessment dated March 15, 2025 and the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment dated May 2, 2025, each prepared by Halcyon Environmental Consultants Inc., have been delivered to Tenant in the form of the executive summary made available to Tenant, and, to Landlord's knowledge, the factual findings therein (including the location, area, depth, and concentrations of the Contamination in the Northwest Corner Area of approximately 4,200 square feet and the Former Dry Dock Area of approximately 1,600 square feet) are accurate, and Landlord has not withheld any environmental report, sampling data, or DEEP correspondence relating to the Premises.

(b) To Landlord's knowledge, there is no Contamination on, at, under, or migrating from the Premises other than the Contamination described in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment and the residual contamination addressed by the ELUR, and no Contamination has migrated, or is migrating, off the Premises.

(c) Landlord has not received any notice of violation, enforcement action, citation, or order from DEEP or any other Governmental Authority relating to the Premises that remains unresolved, and the ELUR is in full force and effect and has not been violated.

(d) The ELUR has not been amended, modified, or supplemented, and no application for the release or modification of the ELUR has been submitted to DEEP.

(e) All Remedial Action taken by Landlord or its predecessors on the Premises has been performed in compliance with the Remediation Standard Regulations and the ELUR, and the engineered barrier required by the ELUR is in place and in good condition, except as disclosed in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment.

(f) Landlord has made available to Tenant all notices, reports, and submissions delivered to or received from DEEP with respect to the Premises, and Landlord has filed all annual ELUR compliance certifications required to date.

### Section 5.2 Tenant's Remediation Obligations.

(a) Tenant shall perform, at its cost (subject to Section 5.3 and Section 5.4), the Remediation described on **Exhibit H** in a good and workmanlike manner, in compliance with the Remediation Standard Regulations, the ELUR, the Remedial Action Plan, the Soil Management Plan, and all other Environmental Requirements, and in coordination with the Project's site work.

(b) Tenant shall engage a Connecticut Licensed Environmental Professional to oversee the Remediation and to certify its completion.

(c) Tenant shall obtain DEEP approval of a Remedial Action Plan and a Soil Management Plan before any ground disturbance on the Premises, and shall obtain a verification report and, where available, DEEP's written determination that the Remediation is complete (whether by a verification of the self-implementing remediation or otherwise).

(d) The Remediation shall be commenced within a reasonable period after the Lease Commencement Date and prosecuted with reasonable diligence in coordination with the Project's construction schedule, and in any event so as not to delay achievement of Milestone 1.

### Section 5.3 Remediation Credit.

(a) Landlord shall grant Tenant a credit in the aggregate amount of **One Million Eight Hundred Thousand Dollars ($1,800,000)** (the "Remediation Credit") against Base Rent, applied as follows:

| Base Rent Month from Rent Commencement Date | Base Rent Due Before Credit | Remediation Credit Applied | Base Rent Payable |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 through 7 | $237,500 per month | $237,500 per month ($1,662,500 in total) | $0 |
| 8 | $237,500 | $137,500 | $100,000 |
| 9 and thereafter | per Section 3.1 | $0 | Full Base Rent |
| **Total** | | **$1,800,000** | |

(b) The Remediation Credit applies only against Base Rent, and not against Percentage Rent, taxes, insurance, or any other amount. The Remediation Credit is a rent credit and not a payment, and shall not be treated as rent paid for purposes of calculating Percentage Rent, the Security Deposit, or any other amount measured by rent.

(c) Tenant may, at its election and by written notice to Landlord given not less than ten (10) days in advance, accelerate the application of any unapplied balance of the Remediation Credit against the next succeeding installments of Base Rent, without regard to the monthly schedule in Section 5.3(a).

(d) If the Rent Commencement Date has not occurred by the date that is forty (40) months after the Lease Commencement Date, Tenant may, at its election, apply any unapplied balance of the Remediation Credit against real property taxes or insurance premiums payable by Tenant with respect to the Premises, and Landlord shall reimburse Tenant for such amounts within thirty (30) days after invoice, with Base Rent thereafter reduced by the amount so reimbursed.

(e) If this Lease expires or is terminated for any reason before the Remediation Credit has been fully applied, Landlord shall pay Tenant the unapplied balance in cash within thirty (30) days after the later of (i) the date of expiration or termination and (ii) the date Tenant delivers a final accounting of the Remediation Credit.

(f) The Remediation Credit is not conditioned on the actual amount of, or on Tenant's completion of, the Remediation, and is not subject to setoff, recapture, or reduction for any reason other than its application against Base Rent as provided in this Section.

### Section 5.4 Remediation Cost Overruns.

(a) Tenant shall be responsible for Remediation Costs up to **Two Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars ($2,400,000)**, which amount reflects the estimated cost of the Remediation set forth in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment ($1,850,000 for the Northwest Corner Area and $550,000 for the Former Dry Dock Area).

(b) Tenant shall be responsible for Remediation Costs in excess of $2,400,000 up to an aggregate of **Three Million Dollars ($3,000,000)**.

(c) Remediation Costs in excess of $3,000,000 shall be allocated as follows:

> (i) to the extent attributable to (A) Contamination that was not identified or delineated in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment, (B) Contamination that has migrated or is migrating from the Premises, (C) the presence of Hazardous Materials in groundwater requiring dewatering or treatment, or (D) any condition existing before the Lease Commencement Date that is unrelated to the footprint of the Project's proposed excavation, in each case Landlord shall bear such excess costs, and if Tenant has incurred them, Landlord shall reimburse Tenant within thirty (30) days after invoice; and
>
> (ii) to the extent attributable to any other cause, including the Project's design, phasing, or means and methods, such excess costs shall be borne equally by Landlord and Tenant, with Landlord's share reimbursed to Tenant within thirty (30) days after invoice or, at Tenant's election, credited against Base Rent.

(d) If the estimate of total Remediation Costs, as revised by the LEP following completion of the Remedial Action Plan design, exceeds Four Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($4,500,000), Tenant may terminate this Lease by written notice delivered within sixty (60) days after receipt of such revised estimate, whereupon the Security Deposit shall be returned to Tenant, Landlord shall pay the unapplied Remediation Credit in cash, and neither party shall have any further obligation except for those that expressly survive.

(e) Landlord's obligations under this Section 5.4 are in addition to, and not in lieu of, Landlord's indemnity obligations under Section 5.8.

### Section 5.5 Work Standards; DEEP Filings; Landlord Cooperation.

(a) All Remediation shall be performed by licensed and insured contractors, in compliance with the Remediation Standard Regulations and the ELUR, and with the engineered barrier and groundwater use prohibitions therein. No potable water supply well shall be installed on the Premises, and all water supply shall be obtained from the municipal water system.

(b) Landlord, as the record fee owner, shall promptly execute and deliver any Remedial Action Plan, Soil Management Plan, Environmental Management Plan, ELUR modification, notice, certification, affidavit, or other submission to DEEP that requires the signature, acknowledgement, or consent of the record owner, and shall not unreasonably withhold, condition, or delay the same; provided that Landlord shall not be required to sign any document that (i) acknowledges liability for a condition caused by Tenant, (ii) is inconsistent with Landlord's obligations under this Lease, or (iii) is not reasonably required for the Remediation, the Approvals, or compliance with the ELUR. Tenant shall reimburse Landlord's reasonable out-of-pocket costs of compliance with this Section 5.5(b), other than attorney's fees incurred to review documents that are consistent with this Lease.

(c) The parties shall jointly authorize and direct the LEP and Halcyon Environmental Consultants Inc. to communicate directly with both parties and with Bayside and its environmental consultant, and Landlord consents to reliance on the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment by Bayside and by any Leasehold Mortgagee.

(d) Tenant shall provide Landlord with copies of all material submissions to and correspondence with DEEP within ten (10) Business Days after delivery or receipt.

### Section 5.6 ELUR Compliance; Ground-Floor Use.

(a) Tenant shall comply in all material respects with the ELUR for the Term, including the prohibition on ground-floor residential use, the engineered barrier requirement, the groundwater use prohibition, and the annual compliance certification requirement.

(b) The parties acknowledge the interpretive ambiguity identified in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment with respect to whether non-habitable ancillary residential spaces on the ground floor — including the residential lobby, leasing office, package room, resident lounge, fitness center, and amenity areas described in the Project program — constitute "residential use" prohibited by the ELUR. Tenant's obligation under Section 9.3 is to limit ground-floor uses as therein provided, and Landlord shall not assert that any such permitted ground-floor use violates the ELUR unless and until DEEP has issued a written determination to that effect.

(c) Landlord shall cooperate with Tenant, at Tenant's cost, in obtaining a written interpretation from DEEP or a modification of the ELUR to permit the ground-floor program described in Section 9.3, and shall join in any application required to be made by the record owner. Landlord shall not unreasonably withhold consent to any ELUR modification that does not increase Landlord's obligations or liability.

(d) If (i) DEEP issues a written determination that any ground-floor use described in Section 9.3 is prohibited by the ELUR, and (ii) no modification of the ELUR permitting such use is obtained within twelve (12) months after such determination, Tenant may, at its election, either redesign the Project to comply, or terminate this Lease by written notice delivered within ninety (90) days after the expiration of such twelve-month period, whereupon the Security Deposit shall be returned to Tenant, Landlord shall pay the unapplied Remediation Credit in cash, and neither party shall have any further obligation except for those that expressly survive. No such termination shall constitute a Milestone Failure or trigger any reverter, forfeiture, or liquidated damages.

### Section 5.7 Engineered Barrier; Soil Management.

Tenant shall design, install, and maintain the engineered barrier (cap) required by the ELUR, consisting of not less than twenty-four (24) inches of documented clean fill or a geomembrane or concrete barrier system approved by DEEP, and shall coordinate site grading, foundation design, and utility installation so as not to compromise the barrier. Tenant shall perform annual inspections and shall report and repair any breach in accordance with the ELUR (notification to DEEP within thirty (30) days and repair within ninety (90) days of discovery). Any refund received by Landlord attributable to taxes paid by Tenant shall be paid to Tenant within thirty (30) days after receipt.

### Section 6.7 Special Assessments.

Tenant shall pay special assessments levied against the Premises during the Term; provided that Tenant may pay any such assessment in installments over the longest period permitted by the assessing authority, and shall not be required to pay any assessment attributable to improvements constructed or to work performed before the Lease Commencement Date, including any assessment relating to the bulkhead demolition that gave rise to the mechanics' lien described on **Exhibit I**.

### Section 6.8 Utilities.

Tenant shall pay all charges for utilities and services supplied to the Premises during the Term. Landlord shall not be obligated to furnish any utility or service, and shall not be liable for any interruption except to the extent caused by Landlord's negligence or willful misconduct.
