## ARTICLE 7. DEVELOPMENT; MILESTONES; FORCE MAJEURE; REVERTER

### Section 7.1 Development Obligation.

(a) Tenant shall develop the Project substantially in accordance with the Project program described in Article 9, the Approvals, and Applicable Law, and shall prosecute construction with reasonable diligence, subject to Force Majeure and the extensions provided in Section 7.4.

(b) Tenant shall have sole control over the design, means and methods, contracting, scheduling, phasing, and value engineering of the Project, subject only to the Approvals and Applicable Law. Landlord's approval rights are limited to those expressly set forth in this Lease (including Section 9.5 as to the design of the public open space) and to any approval required under Applicable Law or as a condition of any Approval.

(c) Tenant may construct the Project in phases. References in this Lease to Phase 1 mean the Residential Tower (including ground-floor commercial and retail space and accessory parking) and references to Phase 2 mean the Office Building.

(d) Tenant shall cause the Project to be constructed in a good and workmanlike manner, in compliance with Applicable Law and the ELUR, and lien-free (subject to Landlord's obligations under Section 17.1(g)).

### Section 7.2 Approvals; Landlord Cooperation.

(a) Tenant shall use diligent efforts to obtain all Approvals. Landlord shall cooperate with Tenant in obtaining Approvals, at no cost to Landlord except as provided in Section 5.5, including by executing applications, consents, and owner's authorizations, by supporting Tenant's applications before the City of Port Calloway Planning and Zoning Commission, Inland Wetlands Commission, Zoning Board of Appeals, and Building Department, and by providing such information regarding Landlord's fee interest and the ELUR as Tenant may reasonably require.

(b) Landlord shall not oppose, and shall not cause or encourage any board, commission, or agency of the City of Port Calloway to oppose, any application for Approvals that is consistent with Applicable Law and the Project program.

(c) If any Approval is denied, revoked, or delayed by reason of the ELUR, Landlord's title, any encumbrance created by Landlord, or any act or omission of Landlord or the City of Port Calloway, the applicable Milestone Deadline shall be extended day for day for the period of such denial, revocation, or delay, in addition to any extension under Section 7.4.

(d) If all Approvals for Phase 1 are denied on a final, non-appealable basis following Tenant's diligent pursuit, and such denial is not attributable to Tenant's design or application, Tenant may terminate this Lease by written notice delivered within ninety (90) days after such final denial, whereupon the Security Deposit shall be returned to Tenant, Landlord shall pay the unapplied Remediation Credit in cash, and neither party shall have any further obligation except for those that expressly survive. No such termination shall constitute a Milestone Failure.

### Section 7.3 Milestones.

Tenant shall achieve each of the following Milestones by the corresponding Milestone Deadline, subject to Section 7.4 and Section 7.2(c):

| Milestone | Requirement | Period from Lease Commencement Date | Deadline if Lease Commencement Date is October 1, 2025 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Milestone 1 | Commencement of Construction: physical pouring of footings for at least one building within the Project, following issuance of all necessary building permits | 18 months | April 1, 2027 |
| Milestone 2 | Completion of Structural Frame: topping-out of the structural steel and/or concrete frame for the Residential Tower | 42 months | April 1, 2029 |
| Milestone 3 | Substantial Completion of Phase 1: issuance of a temporary or permanent certificate of occupancy for the Residential Tower and ground-floor retail space, such that the Residential Tower is ready for residential occupancy and the retail space is available for tenant fit-out | 60 months | October 1, 2030 |
| Milestone 4 | Substantial Completion of Phase 2: issuance of a temporary or permanent certificate of occupancy for the Office Building | 84 months | October 1, 2032 |

### Section 7.4 Force Majeure and Permitting Extensions.

(a) Each Milestone Deadline shall be extended, day for day, for delay in achievement of the applicable Milestone caused by Force Majeure, up to a maximum aggregate extension of twelve (12) months across all Milestones, and shall be further extended for delay attributable to governmental permitting processes beyond Tenant's reasonable control, including delays in the issuance of building permits, zoning approvals, coastal or wetlands approvals, DEEP approvals, or certificates of occupancy, up to an additional six (6) months in the aggregate. The total aggregate extension under this Section 7.4 shall not exceed eighteen (18) months.

(b) "**Force Majeure**" means any event or condition beyond Tenant's reasonable control that actually delays achievement of a Milestone, including: acts of God; unusually severe weather; named tropical storms, hurricanes, nor'easters, and other storm events; tidal flooding and storm surge; changes in Federal Emergency Management Agency flood mapping or floodplain requirements; fire and other casualty; war, terrorism, sabotage, and civil unrest; strikes, lockouts, and labor disputes; governmental orders, moratoria, shutdowns, and delays in the processing or issuance of Approvals (subject to the permitting extension in Section 7.4(a)); epidemics and pandemics; shortages, unavailability, or delay in the delivery of materials, equipment, or labor resulting from supply-chain disruption, tariffs, or trade restrictions; utility failures and utility company delays; the discovery of Hazardous Materials, archaeological resources, or unknown site conditions not identified in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment or the Survey; judicial orders and injunctions; and delays caused by Landlord, its agents, or any Governmental Authority.

(c) Force Majeure does not include Tenant's lack of funds, inability to obtain financing, or general market or economic conditions, except to the extent such conditions manifest as an event described in Section 7.4(b).

(d) Tenant shall give Landlord written notice of any claim of Force Majeure or permitting delay within thirty (30) days after Tenant becomes aware of the event, describing the event and its anticipated duration. Failure to give timely notice shall reduce the extension only by the number of days of delay in giving notice and shall not otherwise prejudice Tenant's entitlement.

(e) Tenant shall use reasonable efforts to mitigate the effects of any Force Majeure event, but shall not be required to incur extraordinary expense, to accelerate construction at premium cost, or to settle any labor dispute on terms it deems commercially unreasonable.

(f) If the parties dispute the duration of any extension, either may submit the matter to an Expert under Section 18.3(c). Pending determination, no Milestone Failure shall be deemed to have occurred with respect to the disputed period.

### Section 7.5 Milestone Failure; Notice; Cure.

(a) If a Milestone Failure occurs, Landlord may deliver written notice (a "**Milestone Notice**") to Tenant and, simultaneously, to each Leasehold Mortgagee, specifying in reasonable detail the Milestone that was not achieved and the basis for the claimed failure.

(b) Tenant shall have one hundred eighty (180) days after receipt of the Milestone Notice (the "**Milestone Cure Period**") to achieve the applicable Milestone or otherwise cure the Milestone Failure.

(c) If Tenant achieves the applicable Milestone within the Milestone Cure Period, this Lease shall remain in full force and effect, Landlord shall have no claim for damages, no reverter shall occur, and the Milestone Notice shall be of no further effect.

(d) No Milestone Failure shall exist, and no Milestone Notice may be delivered, with respect to any period during which the applicable Milestone Deadline is extended under Section 7.2(c) or Section 7.4, or during which Landlord is in default of its obligations under this Lease in a manner that has prevented achievement of the Milestone.

### Section 7.6 Reverter Right; Conditions to Exercise.

(a) Subject to Sections 7.6(b) through 7.6(e), if a Milestone Failure is not cured within the Milestone Cure Period, Landlord may terminate this Lease (a "**Reverter Termination**") by written notice delivered to Tenant and simultaneously to each Leasehold Mortgagee after the expiration of the Milestone Cure Period and after the expiration of all applicable Leasehold Mortgagee cure periods under Section 10.3.

(b) **No automatic termination.** This Lease shall not terminate automatically upon the expiration of the Milestone Cure Period or upon any other event. Termination may occur only upon Landlord's written notice under Section 7.6(a), and only after all conditions in this Section 7.6 have been satisfied. Any provision of the Term Sheet providing for automatic termination upon expiration of the Milestone Cure Period is superseded by this Section 7.6(b).

(c) **Leasehold Mortgagee cure.** No Reverter Termination shall be effective unless and until (i) each Leasehold Mortgagee has received the Milestone Notice simultaneously with Tenant, and (ii) the applicable cure period under Section 10.3(c) (being not less than one hundred eighty (180) days after the Leasehold Mortgagee's receipt of the Milestone Notice) has expired without cure. A Leasehold Mortgagee may cure a Milestone Failure by performing the Milestone, by advancing funds to Tenant, by causing a replacement developer, general contractor, or property manager acceptable to Landlord (such acceptance not to be unreasonably withheld) to be installed and to undertake the Milestone, or by exercise of its New Lease right under Section 10.4.

(d) **No reverter where Mortgagee exercises New Lease.** If any Leasehold Mortgagee exercises its New Lease right under Section 10.4, the Reverter Termination shall be of no force or effect, the Improvements shall be included in the New Lease without additional rent, and Landlord shall have no claim to the Security Deposit except to the extent of draws permitted under Section 8.4 and Section 7.9.

(e) **Reverter subordinate to Leasehold Mortgage.** The reverter right is and shall remain subject and subordinate in all respects to each Leasehold Mortgage and to the rights of each Leasehold Mortgagee under Article 10. Landlord shall not exercise the reverter right in any manner that extinguishes, impairs, or otherwise defeats the security interest of any Leasehold Mortgagee.

### Section 7.7 Compensation on Reverter Termination.

(a) **Payment required.** If a Reverter Termination occurs, Landlord shall pay Tenant, as a condition to Landlord's recovery of possession, an amount (the "**Reverter Compensation**") equal to the greater of:

> (i) the Fair Market Value of the Improvements as of the date of the Reverter Termination, determined under Section 7.7(b); or
>
> (ii) Tenant's Net Hard Costs, determined under Section 7.7(c).

(b) **Fair Market Value determination.** Within twenty (20) days after the Reverter Termination, each party shall appoint a qualified MAI appraiser licensed in Connecticut. Each appraiser shall deliver a written determination of the Fair Market Value of the Improvements within forty-five (45) days after appointment. If the two determinations differ by ten percent (10%) or less of the higher determination, the Fair Market Value shall be their average. If they differ by more than ten percent (10%), the two appraisers shall appoint a third MAI appraiser within ten (10) days, whose sole determination, delivered within forty-five (45) days after appointment, shall be the Fair Market Value. Each party shall bear the cost of its own appraiser, and the parties shall share equally the cost of the third appraiser. The appraisers shall value the Improvements as an undivided whole, in place, as is, in their then-existing condition, without deduction for the value of the Land, the reversion, or any leasehold mortgage, and without regard to the circumstances of the termination.

(c) **Net Hard Costs.** "**Net Hard Costs**" means Tenant's actual, documented, out-of-pocket hard construction costs incurred and paid with respect to the Improvements, as evidenced by paid invoices, certified draw schedules, lien waivers, and the construction lender's records, excluding soft costs, financing costs, developer fees, remediation costs, and rent, reduced by (i) insurance proceeds actually received and retained by Tenant with respect to the Improvements, and (ii) the amount of Landlord Damages determined under Section 7.7(d).

(d) **Landlord Damages.** "**Landlord Damages**" means Landlord's actual, documented, direct damages resulting from the Milestone Failure, limited to (i) reasonable, documented costs incurred to re-market the Premises and to procure a replacement developer, (ii) reasonable out-of-pocket costs and expenses, and (iii) the amount by which Base Rent that would have accrued from the Rent Commencement Date to the date of the Reverter Termination, had the Project been completed in accordance with the Milestone schedule, exceeds Base Rent actually received, which amount shall not exceed twenty-four (24) months of Base Rent at the rate in effect on the date of the Reverter Termination. Landlord Damages shall exclude consequential, indirect, special, incidental, and punitive damages, lost profits (other than as limited in clause (iii)), diminution in the value of the fee, attorneys' fees except as awarded under Section 18.3, and any amount attributable to Landlord's own act, omission, or breach. Landlord shall have a duty to mitigate its damages.

(e) **Payment; possession.** Landlord shall pay the Reverter Compensation within ninety (90) days after its final determination under Section 7.7(b) and Section 7.7(c). Amounts unpaid after such date shall bear interest at eight percent (8%) per annum. Landlord shall not be entitled to possession of the Premises or the Improvements, and Tenant shall not be required to surrender possession, until the Reverter Compensation has been paid in full or deposited into escrow with a nationally recognized title company or escrow agent reasonably acceptable to Tenant. If the Reverter Compensation has not been paid or deposited within one hundred twenty (120) days after its final determination, Tenant may, at its election, (i) rescind the Reverter Termination and continue this Lease in full force and effect as if the Milestone Notice had not been delivered, or (ii) pursue any remedy available at law or in equity, including specific performance.

(f) **No forfeiture.** The parties agree that the reverter right is intended to be a reasonable enforcement mechanism to secure Tenant's performance and not a penalty or forfeiture, and that Landlord shall not be entitled to any Improvement without payment of the Reverter Compensation. If any provision of this Article 7 is determined by a court of competent jurisdiction to be unenforceable as a penalty or an unconscionable forfeiture, such provision shall be reformed and enforced to the maximum extent necessary to make Landlord whole for its actual damages and no more, and Tenant shall in all events be entitled to the Reverter Compensation net of Landlord Damages.

### Section 7.8 Landlord's Election to Purchase.

In lieu of a Reverter Termination, Landlord may elect, by written notice delivered within sixty (60) days after the expiration of all cure periods under Section 7.6, to purchase Tenant's leasehold interest and the Improvements for a price equal to the Reverter Compensation determined under Section 7.7, in which case the closing shall occur within one hundred twenty (120) days after such election, the Leasehold Mortgage shall be paid in full at closing or assumed by Landlord on terms acceptable to the Leasehold Mortgagee, and Tenant shall convey its leasehold interest free and clear of liens and encumbrances arising by, through, or under Tenant.

### Section 7.9 Security Deposit on Reverter Termination.

Upon a Reverter Termination, Landlord may draw upon the Security Deposit only in the amount of Landlord Damages determined under Section 7.7(d) and any Base Rent, Percentage Rent, or other amounts then due and unpaid. Landlord shall return the Security Deposit, or the undrawn balance thereof, to Tenant within ten (10) Business Days after the final determination under Section 7.7, together with any excess drawn amount. The forfeiture of the entire Security Deposit upon a Milestone Failure, as described in the Term Sheet, is superseded by this Section 7.9, and any attempt to retain the Security Deposit other than as provided in this Section 7.9 shall be void.

### Section 7.10 Circumstances Excluding Reverter.

Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Lease, no Milestone Failure shall be deemed to have occurred, and no Reverter Termination shall be permitted, if and to the extent the failure to achieve the applicable Milestone results from: (a) any breach or default by Landlord under this Lease; (b) Force Majeure or permitting delay for which Tenant is entitled to an extension under Section 7.4, regardless of whether the aggregate caps in Section 7.4(a) have been exhausted, where the delay continues beyond the caps and is not attributable to Tenant's lack of diligence; (c) a Casualty or Condemnation; (d) a determination by DEEP or any other Governmental Authority relating to the ELUR, or any denial, revocation, stay, or injunction affecting the Approvals for reasons not attributable to Tenant; (e) any act or omission of Landlord, the City of Port Calloway, or any utility; or (f) Tenant's achievement of the applicable Milestone before the Reverter Termination becomes effective. In any such case, the Milestone Deadline shall be extended by the period of the excused delay.

### Section 7.11 Effect of a Reverter Termination.

Upon a Reverter Termination (and subject to Section 7.7(e)): (a) rent and all other amounts shall be prorated to the date of termination; (b) Landlord shall take the Premises and the Improvements subject to the Permitted Exceptions and subject to all subleases, licenses, and occupancy agreements entered into in the ordinary course, which Landlord shall recognize; (c) at Landlord's election, Tenant shall assign to Landlord, without representation or warranty other than as to title, such service contracts, warranties, guaranties, permits, and plans as relate to the Premises, and Landlord shall assume the obligations accruing after the termination date; (d) Tenant shall deliver as-built drawings, operation and maintenance manuals, and warranties in its possession; (e) Tenant may remove its Trade Fixtures and Personal Property within ninety (90) days after termination, repairing any damage caused by removal; and (f) the obligations of the parties that expressly survive shall continue. No merger of the leasehold estate into the fee shall occur by reason of any such transfer.

### Section 7.12 Nature of the Milestone Covenants.

The Milestones are covenants of Tenant, the sole and exclusive remedy for the breach of which is set forth in this Article 7. The Milestones are not conditions subsequent to the effectiveness of this Lease or to the vesting of Tenant's leasehold estate, and no failure to achieve a Milestone shall, by itself, divest Tenant of its leasehold estate or of any Improvement without payment of the Reverter Compensation.

## ARTICLE 8. SECURITY DEPOSIT

### Section 8.1 Amount.

Tenant shall deliver to Landlord, on or before the Lease Commencement Date, a security deposit in the amount of **Five Million Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars ($5,700,000)**, equal to twenty-four (24) months of the initial monthly Base Rent (the "Security Deposit").

### Section 8.2 Form.

(a) The Security Deposit shall be evidenced by an irrevocable standby letter of credit substantially in the form of **Exhibit F**, issued by a commercial bank organized under the laws of the United States or any state thereof, having a minimum long-term credit rating of A- from S&P Global Ratings or A3 from Moody's Investors Service (or an equivalent rating from a nationally recognized rating agency), naming Landlord as beneficiary, permitting partial draws, and permitting transfer to a successor landlord or to the Leasehold Mortgagee. Landlord shall accept a letter of credit issued by a state-chartered bank meeting such rating requirement, and nothing in this Lease or in Resolution No. 2025-047 shall be construed to require a federally chartered institution.

(b) Tenant may, at its election, satisfy the Security Deposit in whole or in part by delivery of cash, in which case Landlord shall hold the cash in a segregated interest-bearing account and shall pay interest to Tenant annually. Landlord may commingle the cash deposit with its general funds only if it pays interest to Tenant at the rate actually earned.

### Section 8.3 Reduction.

(a) The Security Deposit shall be reduced to **Two Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars ($2,850,000)** upon Tenant's demonstration that the Project has achieved and maintained an Occupancy Rate of ninety percent (90%) or greater for twenty-four (24) consecutive months.

(b) "**Occupancy Rate**" means, as of any date, the percentage obtained by dividing (i) the aggregate rentable square footage of all residential units, office space, and retail space in the completed Project that is leased to and occupied by tenants paying rent (excluding model units, leasing offices, amenity space, and space occupied by Tenant or its Affiliates without paying rent) by (ii) the aggregate rentable square footage of all residential units, office space, and retail space in the completed Project that has been delivered and is available for lease.

(c) Tenant shall demonstrate satisfaction of the condition by delivering a certificate of its chief financial officer, together with a rent roll and such supporting information as Landlord may reasonably request. Landlord shall have ten (10) Business Days after receipt to object in writing, specifying in reasonable detail the basis for its objection. If Landlord does not object within such period, the reduction shall be deemed approved. If Landlord objects, the parties shall submit the matter to an Expert under Section 18.3(c), and any adjustment shall be made within ten (10) Business Days after the determination.

(d) The reduction is a one-time reduction. If the Occupancy Rate later falls below ninety percent (90%), the Security Deposit shall not be increased, and the reduction shall not be revoked.

(e) Tenant may effect the reduction by delivering a replacement letter of credit in the reduced amount (or by directing the issuing bank to reduce the stated amount) and, if a cash deposit was provided, Landlord shall return the excess within ten (10) Business Days after the reduction is approved.

### Section 8.4 Draws.

(a) Landlord may draw upon the Security Deposit only upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an uncured Tenant Event of Default, and only in the amount of the monetary obligations then due and unpaid, or of the actual, documented, direct damages sustained by Landlord as a result of the Tenant Event of Default, in each case determined in accordance with this Lease.

(b) Landlord shall deliver notice of any intended draw to Tenant and to each Leasehold Mortgagee not less than ten (10) Business Days before presentation of the draw, and shall not draw (i) any amount disputed by Tenant in good faith and as to which Tenant has commenced a dispute under Section 18.3, (ii) any amount that a Leasehold Mortgagee has cured or has elected to cure within its cure period under Section 10.3, or (iii) any amount in excess of the amounts permitted under Section 8.4(a).

(c) Amounts drawn shall be applied to the Tenant obligations giving rise to the draw, and Landlord shall deliver to Tenant a written accounting within ten (10) Business Days after any draw.

(d) If any draw is determined to have been improper, Landlord shall repay the amount, with interest at eight percent (8%) per annum, within ten (10) Business Days after such determination.

### Section 8.5 Replenishment.

Tenant shall replenish any properly drawn amount within thirty (30) days after a draw. If Tenant disputes a draw in good faith, replenishment of the disputed portion shall be deferred until the dispute is resolved, and Tenant shall then replenish within thirty (30) days after resolution.

### Section 8.6 Maintenance of the Security Deposit.

Tenant shall maintain the Security Deposit in full force and effect throughout the Term. If the rating of the issuing bank falls below the required level, Tenant shall, within sixty (60) days after notice from Landlord, deliver a replacement letter of credit from a qualifying institution; Tenant shall not be in default under this Section 8.6 if it is diligently pursuing a replacement and delivers it within such period. If the letter of credit has an expiration date, Tenant shall deliver a renewal or replacement not later than thirty (30) days before expiration, and Tenant shall not be in default if the issuing bank fails to renew through no fault of Tenant and Tenant delivers a replacement within thirty (30) days after such failure.

### Section 8.7 Return.

Landlord shall return the Security Deposit, or the undrawn balance, to Tenant within thirty (30) days after the expiration of the Term or the earlier termination of this Lease, less any amount properly applied under Section 8.4 and Section 7.9. Landlord shall not be entitled to hold the Security Deposit after the expiration of such period, and any retention thereafter shall bear interest at eight percent (8%) per annum.

### Section 8.8 Transfers.

Upon a permitted Transfer under Article 11, Landlord shall, at Tenant's request and cost, cooperate in the transfer or replacement of the Security Deposit to or for the benefit of the transferee, and Landlord shall not require an increase in the Security Deposit by reason of any Transfer.

(d) No Milestone Failure shall exist, and no Milestone Notice may be delivered, with respect to any period during which the applicable Milestone Deadline is extended under Section 7.2(c) or Section 7.4, or during which Landlord is in default of its obligations under this Lease in a manner that has prevented achievement of the Milestone.

### Section 7.6 Reverter Right; Conditions to Exercise.

(a) Subject to Sections 7.6(b) through 7.6(e), if a Milestone Failure is not cured within the Milestone Cure Period, Landlord may terminate this Lease (a "**Reverter Termination**") by written notice delivered to Tenant and simultaneously to each Leasehold Mortgagee after the expiration of the Milestone Cure Period and after the expiration of all applicable Leasehold Mortgagee cure periods under Section 10.3.

(b) **No automatic termination.** This Lease shall not terminate automatically upon the expiration of the Milestone Cure Period or upon any other event. Termination may occur only upon Landlord's written notice under Section 7.6(a), and only after all conditions in this Section 7.6 have been satisfied. Any provision of the Term Sheet providing for automatic termination upon expiration of the Milestone Cure Period is superseded by this Section 7.6(b).

(c) **Leasehold Mortgagee cure.** No Reverter Termination shall be effective unless and until (i) each Leasehold Mortgagee has received the Milestone Notice simultaneously with Tenant, and (ii) the applicable cure period under Section 10.3(c) (being not less than one hundred eighty (180) days after the Leasehold Mortgagee's receipt of the Milestone Notice) has expired without cure. A Leasehold Mortgagee may cure a Milestone Failure by performing the Milestone, by advancing funds to Tenant, by causing a replacement developer, general contractor, or property manager acceptable to Landlord (such acceptance not to be unreasonably withheld) to be installed and to undertake the Milestone, or by exercise of its New Lease right under Section 10.4.

(d) **No reverter where Mortgagee exercises New Lease.** If any Leasehold Mortgagee exercises its New Lease right under Section 10.4, the Reverter Termination shall be of no force or effect, the Improvements shall be included in the New Lease without additional rent, and Landlord shall have no claim to the Security Deposit except to the extent of draws permitted under Section 8.4 and Section 7.9.

(e) **Reverter subordinate to Leasehold Mortgage.** The reverter right is and shall remain subject and subordinate in all respects to each Leasehold Mortgage and to the rights of each Leasehold Mortgagee under Article 10. Landlord shall not exercise the reverter right in any manner that extinguishes, impairs, or otherwise defeats the security interest of any Leasehold Mortgagee.

### Section 7.7 Compensation on Reverter Termination.

(a) **Payment required.** If a Reverter Termination occurs, Landlord shall pay Tenant, as a condition to Landlord's recovery of possession, an amount (the "**Reverter Compensation**") equal to the greater of:

> (i) the Fair Market Value of the Improvements as of the date of the Reverter Termination, determined under Section 7.7(b); or
>
> (ii) Tenant's Net Hard Costs, determined under Section 7.7(c).

(b) **Fair Market Value determination.** Within twenty (20) days after the Reverter Termination, each party shall appoint a qualified MAI appraiser licensed in Connecticut. Each appraiser shall deliver a written determination of the Fair Market Value of the Improvements within forty-five (45) days after appointment. If the two determinations differ by ten percent (10%) or less of the higher determination, the Fair Market Value shall be their average. If they differ by more than ten percent (10%), the two appraisers shall appoint a third MAI appraiser within ten (10) days, whose sole determination, delivered within forty-five (45) days after appointment, shall be the Fair Market Value. Each party shall bear the cost of its own appraiser, and the parties shall share equally the cost of the third appraiser. The appraisers shall value the Improvements as an undivided whole, in place, as is, in their then-existing condition, without deduction for the value of the Land, the reversion, or any leasehold mortgage, and without regard to the circumstances of the termination.

(c) **Net Hard Costs.** "**Net Hard Costs**" means Tenant's actual, documented, out-of-pocket hard construction costs incurred and paid with respect to the Improvements, as evidenced by paid invoices, certified draw schedules, lien waivers, and the construction lender's records, excluding soft costs, financing costs, developer fees, remediation costs, and rent, reduced by (i) insurance proceeds actually received and retained by Tenant with respect to the Improvements, and (ii) the amount of Landlord Damages determined under Section 7.7(d).

(d) **Landlord Damages.** "**Landlord Damages**" means Landlord's actual, documented, direct damages resulting from the Milestone Failure, limited to (i) reasonable, documented costs incurred to re-market the Premises and to procure a replacement developer, (ii) reasonable out-of-pocket costs and expenses, and (iii) the amount by which Base Rent that would have accrued from the Rent Commencement Date to the date of the Reverter Termination, had the Project been completed in accordance with the Milestone schedule, exceeds Base Rent actually received, which amount shall not exceed twenty-four (24) months of Base Rent at the rate in effect on the date of the Reverter Termination. Landlord Damages shall exclude consequential, indirect, special, incidental, and punitive damages, lost profits (other than as limited in clause (iii)), diminution in the value of the fee, attorneys' fees except as awarded under Section 18.3, and any amount attributable to Landlord's own act, omission, or breach. Landlord shall have a duty to mitigate its damages.

(e) **Payment; possession.** Landlord shall pay the Reverter Compensation within ninety (90) days after its final determination under Section 7.7(b) and Section 7.7(c). Amounts unpaid after such date shall bear interest at eight percent (8%) per annum. Landlord shall not be entitled to possession of the Premises or the Improvements, and Tenant shall not be required to surrender possession, until the Reverter Compensation has been paid in full or deposited into escrow with a nationally recognized title company or escrow agent reasonably acceptable to Tenant. If the Reverter Compensation has not been paid or deposited within one hundred twenty (120) days after its final determination, Tenant may, at its election, (i) rescind the Reverter Termination and continue this Lease in full force and effect as if the Milestone Notice had not been delivered, or (ii) pursue any remedy available at law or in equity, including specific performance.

(f) **No forfeiture.** The parties agree that the reverter right is intended to be a reasonable enforcement mechanism to secure Tenant's performance and not a penalty or forfeiture, and that Landlord shall not be entitled to any Improvement without payment of the Reverter Compensation. If any provision of this Article 7 is determined by a court of competent jurisdiction to be unenforceable as a penalty or an unconscionable forfeiture, such provision shall be reformed and enforced to the maximum extent necessary to make Landlord whole for its actual damages and no more, and Tenant shall in all events be entitled to the Reverter Compensation net of Landlord Damages.

### Section 7.8 Landlord's Election to Purchase.

In lieu of a Reverter Termination, Landlord may elect, by written notice delivered within sixty (60) days after the expiration of all cure periods under Section 7.6, to purchase Tenant's leasehold interest and the Improvements for a price equal to the Reverter Compensation determined under Section 7.7, in which case the closing shall occur within one hundred twenty (120) days after such election, the Leasehold Mortgage shall be paid in full at closing or assumed by Landlord on terms acceptable to the Leasehold Mortgagee, and Tenant shall convey its leasehold interest free and clear of liens and encumbrances arising by, through, or under Tenant.

### Section 7.9 Security Deposit on Reverter Termination.

Upon a Reverter Termination, Landlord may draw upon the Security Deposit only in the amount of Landlord Damages determined under Section 7.7(d) and any Base Rent, Percentage Rent, or other amounts then due and unpaid. Landlord shall return the Security Deposit, or the undrawn balance thereof, to Tenant within ten (10) Business Days after the final determination under Section 7.7, together with any excess drawn amount. The forfeiture of the entire Security Deposit upon a Milestone Failure, as described in the Term Sheet, is superseded by this Section 7.9, and any attempt to retain the Security Deposit other than as provided in this Section 7.9 shall be void.

### Section 7.10 Circumstances Excluding Reverter.

Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Lease, no Milestone Failure shall be deemed to have occurred, and no Reverter Termination shall be permitted, if and to the extent the failure to achieve the applicable Milestone results from: (a) any breach or default by Landlord under this Lease; (b) Force Majeure or permitting delay for which Tenant is entitled to an extension under Section 7.4, regardless of whether the aggregate caps in Section 7.4(a) have been exhausted, where the delay continues beyond the caps and is not attributable to Tenant's lack of diligence; (c) a Casualty or Condemnation; (d) a determination by DEEP or any other Governmental Authority relating to the ELUR, or any denial, revocation, stay, or injunction affecting the Approvals for reasons not attributable to Tenant; (e) any act or omission of Landlord, the City of Port Calloway, or any utility; or (f) Tenant's achievement of the applicable Milestone before the Reverter Termination becomes effective. In any such case, the Milestone Deadline shall be extended by the period of the excused delay.

### Section 7.11 Effect of a Reverter Termination.

Upon a Reverter Termination (and subject to Section 7.7(e)): (a) rent and all other amounts shall be prorated to the date of termination; (b) Landlord shall take the Premises and the Improvements subject to the Permitted Exceptions and subject to all subleases, licenses, and occupancy agreements entered into in the ordinary course, which Landlord shall recognize; (c) at Landlord's election, Tenant shall assign to Landlord, without representation or warranty other than as to title, such service contracts, warranties, guaranties, permits, and plans as relate to the Premises, and Landlord shall assume the obligations accruing after the termination date; (d) Tenant shall deliver as-built drawings, operation and maintenance manuals, and warranties in its possession; (e) Tenant may remove its Trade Fixtures and Personal Property within ninety (90) days after termination, repairing any damage caused by removal; and (f) the obligations of the parties that expressly survive shall continue. No merger of the leasehold estate into the fee shall occur by reason of any such transfer.

### Section 7.12 Nature of the Milestone Covenants.

The Milestones are covenants of Tenant, the sole and exclusive remedy for the breach of which is set forth in this Article 7. The Milestones are not conditions subsequent to the effectiveness of this Lease or to the vesting of Tenant's leasehold estate, and no failure to achieve a Milestone shall, by itself, divest Tenant of its leasehold estate or of any Improvement without payment of the Reverter Compensation.

## ARTICLE 8. SECURITY DEPOSIT

### Section 8.1 Amount.

Tenant shall deliver to Landlord, on or before the Lease Commencement Date, a security deposit in the amount of **Five Million Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars ($5,700,000)**, equal to twenty-four (24) months of the initial monthly Base Rent (the "Security Deposit").

### Section 8.2 Form.

(a) The Security Deposit shall be evidenced by an irrevocable standby letter of credit substantially in the form of **Exhibit F**, issued by a commercial bank organized under the laws of the United States or any state thereof, having a minimum long-term credit rating of A- from S&P Global Ratings or A3 from Moody's Investors Service (or an equivalent rating from a nationally recognized rating agency), naming Landlord as beneficiary, permitting partial draws, and permitting transfer to a successor landlord or to the Leasehold Mortgagee. Landlord shall accept a letter of credit issued by a state-chartered bank meeting such rating requirement, and nothing in this Lease or in Resolution No. 2025-047 shall be construed to require a federally chartered institution.

(b) Tenant may, at its election, satisfy the Security Deposit in whole or in part by delivery of cash, in which case Landlord shall hold the cash in a segregated interest-bearing account and shall pay interest to Tenant annually. Landlord may commingle the cash deposit with its general funds only if it pays interest to Tenant at the rate actually earned.

### Section 8.3 Reduction.

(a) The Security Deposit shall be reduced to **Two Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars ($2,850,000)** upon Tenant's demonstration that the Project has achieved and maintained an Occupancy Rate of ninety percent (90%) or greater for twenty-four (24) consecutive months.

(b) "**Occupancy Rate**" means, as of any date, the percentage obtained by dividing (i) the aggregate rentable square footage of all residential units, office space, and retail space in the completed Project that is leased to and occupied by tenants paying rent (excluding model units, leasing offices, amenity space, and space occupied by Tenant or its Affiliates without paying rent) by (ii) the aggregate rentable square footage of all residential units, office space, and retail space in the completed Project that has been delivered and is available for lease.

(c) Tenant shall demonstrate satisfaction of the condition by delivering a certificate of its chief financial officer, together with a rent roll and such supporting information as Landlord may reasonably request. Landlord shall have ten (10) Business Days after receipt to object in writing, specifying in reasonable detail the basis for its objection. If Landlord does not object within such period, the reduction shall be deemed approved. If Landlord objects, the parties shall submit the matter to an Expert under Section 18.3(c), and any adjustment shall be made within ten (10) Business Days after the determination.

(d) The reduction is a one-time reduction. If the Occupancy Rate later falls below ninety percent (90%), the Security Deposit shall not be increased, and the reduction shall not be revoked.

(e) Tenant may effect the reduction by delivering a replacement letter of credit in the reduced amount (or by directing the issuing bank to reduce the stated amount) and, if a cash deposit was provided, Landlord shall return the excess within ten (10) Business Days after the reduction is approved.

### Section 8.4 Draws.

(a) Landlord may draw upon the Security Deposit only upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an uncured Tenant Event of Default, and only in the amount of the monetary obligations then due and unpaid, or of the actual, documented, direct damages sustained by Landlord as a result of the Tenant Event of Default, in each case determined in accordance with this Lease.

(b) Landlord shall deliver notice of any intended draw to Tenant and to each Leasehold Mortgagee not less than ten (10) Business Days before presentation of the draw, and shall not draw (i) any amount disputed by Tenant in good faith and as to which Tenant has commenced a dispute under Section 18.3, (ii) any amount that a Leasehold Mortgagee has cured or has elected to cure within its cure period under Section 10.3, or (iii) any amount in excess of the amounts permitted under Section 8.4(a).

(c) Amounts drawn shall be applied to the Tenant obligations giving rise to the draw, and Landlord shall deliver to Tenant a written accounting within ten (10) Business Days after any draw.

(d) If any draw is determined to have been improper, Landlord shall repay the amount, with interest at eight percent (8%) per annum, within ten (10) Business Days after such determination.

### Section 8.5 Replenishment.

Tenant shall replenish any properly drawn amount within thirty (30) days after a draw. If Tenant disputes a draw in good faith, replenishment of the disputed portion shall be deferred until the dispute is resolved, and Tenant shall then replenish within thirty (30) days after resolution.

### Section 8.6 Maintenance of the Security Deposit.

Tenant shall maintain the Security Deposit in full force and effect throughout the Term. If the rating of the issuing bank falls below the required level, Tenant shall, within sixty (60) days after notice from Landlord, deliver a replacement letter of credit from a qualifying institution; Tenant shall not be in default under this Section 8.6 if it is diligently pursuing a replacement and delivers it within such period. If the letter of credit has an expiration date, Tenant shall deliver a renewal or replacement not later than thirty (30) days before expiration, and Tenant shall not be in default if the issuing bank fails to renew through no fault of Tenant and Tenant delivers a replacement within thirty (30) days after such failure.

### Section 8.7 Return.

Landlord shall return the Security Deposit, or the undrawn balance, to Tenant within thirty (30) days after the expiration of the Term or the earlier termination of this Lease, less any amount properly applied under Section 8.4 and Section 7.9. Landlord shall not be entitled to hold the Security Deposit after the expiration of such period, and any retention thereafter shall bear interest at eight percent (8%) per annum.

### Section 8.8 Transfers.

Upon a permitted Transfer under Article 11, Landlord shall, at Tenant's request and cost, cooperate in the transfer or replacement of the Security Deposit to or for the benefit of the transferee, and Landlord shall not require an increase in the Security Deposit by reason of any Transfer.
