## ARTICLE 9. USE; OPERATIONS; AFFORDABLE HOUSING; OPEN SPACE; MAINTENANCE

### Section 9.1 Permitted Uses.

The Premises may be used for the following purposes and for no other purpose: (a) residential apartments for rent only (no condominium, cooperative, or for-sale units); (b) Class A office; (c) ground-floor retail, excluding adult entertainment establishments, firearms sales, pawnshops, and gasoline service stations; (d) restaurants, including those licensed for liquor service by the Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection; (e) accessory structured and below-grade parking; and (f) uses ancillary to the foregoing, including amenity space, leasing offices, management offices, and building systems.

### Section 9.2 Prohibited Uses.

No industrial, manufacturing, warehousing, or self-storage use shall be permitted. No use shall be permitted that (a) violates the ELUR, the Remediation Standard Regulations, the Affordable Housing Covenant, or any other Applicable Law; (b) constitutes a nuisance or unreasonably interferes with the use and enjoyment of neighboring property; (c) creates a material risk of fire, explosion, or release of Hazardous Materials beyond the quantities customary for the operation of a mixed-use project; or (d) would impair the insurability of the Premises or the Improvements.

### Section 9.3 Ground-Floor Uses; ELUR Restriction.

(a) Tenant shall not construct dwelling units on the ground floor of any building within the Project, and no habitable residential space shall be located at or below finished grade, in compliance with the ELUR.

(b) The ground floor of the Residential Tower may be used for retail and commercial tenancies and for non-habitable ancillary building functions, including the residential lobby, leasing office, package and mail room, building management office, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing rooms, parking, loading, bicycle storage, and resident amenity areas (including a fitness center and resident lounge).

(c) The parties acknowledge the interpretive ambiguity described in Section 5.6(b). Tenant's rights under Section 5.6(d) and Section 5.6(e) (redesign or termination) are Tenant's sole remedies for any determination by DEEP that any such ground-floor ancillary use is prohibited by the ELUR, and no such determination shall constitute a Tenant Event of Default.

(d) Affordable dwelling units shall be located exclusively on the second floor and above, in accordance with the recommendation of Halcyon Environmental Consultants Inc. in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment.

### Section 9.4 Affordable Housing.

(a) **Requirement.** Not less than fifteen percent (15%) of the residential dwelling units constructed within the Project shall be designated as affordable housing units available to households earning at or below eighty percent (80%) of Area Median Income, for the duration of the Term (the "Affordable Units"). The requirement shall not be reduced, eliminated, or relocated off the Premises, and shall be documented in a recorded declaration or regulatory agreement reasonably satisfactory to Landlord and consistent with the recorded Affordable Housing Restrictive Covenant (Volume 408, Page 230 of the Port Calloway Land Records).

(b) **Calculation.** The number of Affordable Units shall be calculated on the basis of the total number of residential dwelling units in the Project as finally designed, rounded up to the next whole unit. If the total unit count changes during the Term by reason of renovation, conversion, or partial demolition, the fifteen percent (15%) requirement shall be recalculated on the basis of the revised unit count, and Tenant shall designate or de-designate units so as to maintain at least fifteen percent (15%) Affordable Units.

(c) **Area Median Income.** Area Median Income shall be determined annually by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development for the metropolitan statistical area applicable to the City of Port Calloway. The parties acknowledge that the recorded Affordable Housing Restrictive Covenant identifies the New Haven-Milford, Connecticut Metropolitan Statistical Area, that the Term Sheet refers to the "Port Calloway Metropolitan Statistical Area," and that the ALTA/NSPS Survey narrative refers to the Bridgeport-Stamford-Norwalk HUD Metro Fair Market Rent Area. The recorded covenant governs, and, if HUD changes the applicable geographic area in which Port Calloway is located, the successor HUD area applicable to Port Calloway shall govern. The parties shall execute an amended or supplemental declaration to conform the recorded covenant to the HUD area actually applicable, at Tenant's cost, upon request of either party.

(d) **Distribution and Unit Mix.** Affordable Units shall be distributed proportionately across unit types (studio, one-bedroom, two-bedroom, and larger units) and shall not be concentrated on any single floor or in any single building segment, to the extent consistent with Applicable Law and the recorded covenant.

(e) **Marketing, Verification, and Compliance.** Tenant shall market Affordable Units in accordance with an affirmative marketing plan, verify household income at initial occupancy and annually thereafter, and deliver to Landlord an annual compliance certificate with a rent roll identifying the Affordable Units, unit sizes, rents charged, and household income bands. Tenant may engage a qualified compliance administrator, and its reasonable costs shall be an operating expense of the Project.

(f) **Enforcement.** If Landlord believes Tenant is not in compliance with this Section 9.4, Landlord shall deliver written notice specifying the alleged non-compliance, and Tenant shall have sixty (60) days to cure (or, if the non-compliance cannot reasonably be cured within sixty (60) days, to commence cure and diligently pursue it to completion). Landlord's sole remedies for non-compliance with this Section 9.4 shall be specific performance and injunctive relief. Non-compliance with this Section 9.4 shall not constitute a Tenant Event of Default, shall not give rise to any right of termination, reverter, or forfeiture, and shall not entitle Landlord to draw upon the Security Deposit.

(g) **No Reduction by Landlord.** Landlord shall not amend, modify, release, or subordinate the Affordable Housing Restrictive Covenant in any manner that would reduce the requirement, and shall not consent to any such reduction.

### Section 9.5 Public Open Space.

(a) The Project shall include not less than eight thousand (8,000) square feet of publicly accessible open space on the waterfront (eastern) side of the Premises, designed and maintained by Tenant at its sole cost, and connected to the existing public pedestrian promenade.

(b) The design and programming of the public open space shall be subject to Landlord's reasonable approval, exercised concurrently with, and within the same time period as, the City's site plan review process. If Landlord does not deliver written objections within thirty (30) days after Tenant's submission of the open space design, the design shall be deemed approved. Landlord's approval shall not be conditioned on any element that would materially increase Tenant's cost or reduce the developable area of the Premises beyond the requirements of the Approvals.

(c) The public open space shall not be dedicated to the public, shall not be conveyed to Landlord or the City, and shall remain part of the Premises and, upon the expiration or termination of this Lease, shall pass to Landlord with the Improvements without additional compensation, subject to Section 16.2.

(d) Tenant may establish reasonable rules and hours for the public open space consistent with public access and the pedestrian easement, may close the space temporarily for maintenance, emergencies, or events, and shall not be required to accept or host any event or programming proposed by Landlord or the City except as Tenant may agree.

(e) Landlord shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Tenant from and against all claims, liabilities, losses, and expenses arising from the use of the public pedestrian access easement, the waterfront promenade, and the public open space by members of the public, except to the extent caused by Tenant's negligence in the maintenance of the public open space or by a condition created by Tenant. Landlord and the City shall maintain their respective insurance covering the promenade and the easement areas, and each party waives subrogation against the other to the extent of insurance proceeds received.

### Section 9.6 Maintenance and Repair; Bulkhead.

(a) Tenant shall maintain, repair, and replace the Premises and the Improvements in good order, condition, and repair throughout the Term, reasonable wear and tear, Casualty, and Condemnation excepted, and shall keep the Premises free of liens, rubbish, and unsafe conditions.

(b) **Bulkhead.** The parties acknowledge that the approximately 480 linear feet of bulkhead along the eastern boundary is in fair to poor condition, as described in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment and the Survey, and that its rehabilitation or replacement is not included in the environmental remediation cost estimates. Tenant shall be responsible for the cost of rehabilitating or replacing the bulkhead as necessary for the construction and operation of the Project; provided, however, that Landlord shall reimburse Tenant for the portion of such cost attributable to the deteriorated condition of the bulkhead existing as of the Lease Commencement Date (as distinguished from the cost attributable to the Project's design, the required design loads, flood and coastal resilience requirements, and Tenant's improvements), as determined by an independent marine structural engineer jointly engaged by the parties within sixty (60) days after the Lease Commencement Date. If the parties cannot agree on the engineer, the engineer shall be appointed by the Expert procedure in Section 18.3(c). Landlord shall pay its share within thirty (30) days after the engineer's determination, or, at Tenant's election, Landlord's share shall be credited against Base Rent. Landlord's obligation under this Section 9.6(b) is in addition to, and not in lieu of, Landlord's obligations under Section 17.1(g) with respect to the pending mechanics' lien, and does not extend to the cost of bulkhead maintenance or replacement attributable to conditions arising after the Lease Commencement Date.

(c) Tenant shall be responsible for all maintenance, repair, and replacement of the bulkhead and all waterfront structures after the Lease Commencement Date, including compliance with any permit or condition applicable to the pedestrian easement area.

### Section 9.7 Operational Standards.

Tenant shall operate the Project in a first-class manner consistent with institutional-quality mixed-use properties in the region, shall provide customary management, security, cleaning, and life-safety services, and may engage Affiliates as manager, leasing agent, or developer without Landlord's consent, provided that any such engagement is on arm's-length terms.

### Section 9.8 Compliance with Laws; Accessibility.

Tenant shall cause the Project to comply with all Applicable Law, including the Connecticut State Building Code, the Connecticut Fire Safety Code, the accessibility provisions of the Americans with Disabilities Act and the Connecticut Fair Housing Act, floodplain management requirements, and the ELUR. Tenant shall maintain the minimum finished floor elevation required by the Approvals and Applicable Law, and the parties acknowledge that Tenant may elect to construct the ground floor at a finished floor elevation above fifteen (15) feet NAVD88 in order to address sea level rise and coastal resilience standards, including the standards described in Section 5 of the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment and Connecticut Public Act 23-167; no such election shall require Landlord's consent or constitute a breach of this Lease.

### Section 9.9 Signage.

Tenant may install building identification, retail, and directional signage consistent with the Approvals and applicable sign regulations, without Landlord's consent. Any signage that advertises Landlord or the City shall be subject to Landlord's prior written approval.

### Section 9.10 Landlord Access.

Landlord and its agents may enter the Premises for inspection, to perform its obligations, or to comply with Applicable Law, upon not less than forty-eight (48) hours' prior written notice (except in an emergency, in which case notice shall be given as soon as practicable), at reasonable times, in a manner that does not unreasonably interfere with the operation of the Project, and subject to Tenant's reasonable security and confidentiality requirements. Landlord shall treat as confidential all information regarding Tenant's operations, revenues, tenants, and financing obtained through any entry, and shall not disclose the same except as required by law or in connection with the enforcement of this Lease.

### Section 9.11 Tenant's Personal Property and Fixtures.

All Improvements shall be and remain Tenant's property during the Term (subject to the Leasehold Mortgage), and Tenant shall have the right to finance, encumber, insure, replace, alter, and (subject to Article 16) remove its Trade Fixtures and Personal Property.

## ARTICLE 10. LEASEHOLD MORTGAGE AND LENDER PROTECTIONS

### Section 10.1 Right to Encumber.

(a) Tenant may, without Landlord's consent, joinder, or approval, and without payment of any fee, charge, or other consideration to Landlord, grant one or more Leasehold Mortgages encumbering Tenant's entire leasehold interest in the Premises together with the Improvements, fixtures, and appurtenances, to any Qualified Mortgagee. No approval, consent, or other condition from Landlord shall be required for the recording, enforcement, foreclosure, or assignment of any Leasehold Mortgage.

(b) Landlord shall, upon request, execute and deliver a commercially reasonable consent to the Leasehold Mortgage, an estoppel certificate under Section 18.4, and the SNDA under Section 10.7, and shall reasonably cooperate with any Leasehold Mortgagee's due diligence, including by providing copies of this Lease, the Permitted Exceptions, and such title, survey, and environmental materials as are in Landlord's possession.

### Section 10.2 Notices to Leasehold Mortgagee.

Landlord shall deliver to each Leasehold Mortgagee, simultaneously with delivery to Tenant, a copy of every notice of default, notice of termination, Milestone Notice, notice of Landlord's exercise of the reverter right or of the right of first refusal, and any other notice materially affecting Tenant's leasehold interest, at the address designated by such Leasehold Mortgagee in writing (initially, Bayside Federal Lending Corp., 200 Atlantic Boulevard, Stamford, Connecticut 06902, Attention: Sandra Milliken, Senior Vice President, Commercial Real Estate Lending, with a copy to Bayside's counsel as designated). Failure to deliver any such notice to a Leasehold Mortgagee shall render the notice ineffective as to such Leasehold Mortgagee and shall suspend the running of Landlord's remedies until a copy is delivered.

### Section 10.3 Leasehold Mortgagee Cure Rights.

(a) **Monetary defaults.** Each Leasehold Mortgagee shall have sixty (60) days after its receipt of notice of any monetary default by Tenant to cure such default on Tenant's behalf.

(b) **Non-monetary defaults.** Each Leasehold Mortgagee shall have ninety (90) days after its receipt of notice of any non-monetary default by Tenant to cure such default, or, if such cure cannot reasonably be completed within ninety (90) days, to commence cure within such period and thereafter diligently and continuously prosecute the cure to completion, in which case the cure period shall extend for such time as is reasonably necessary, not to exceed an additional one hundred eighty (180) days.

(c) **Milestone Failures.** Each Leasehold Mortgagee shall have one hundred eighty (180) days after its receipt of a Milestone Notice to cure the Milestone Failure, by any of the means described in Section 7.6(c).

(d) **Additional, not concurrent.** The cure periods in this Section 10.3 are in addition to, and shall not run concurrently with, the cure periods afforded to Tenant under this Lease. No termination, reverter, forfeiture, or exercise of any remedy by Landlord that would divest Tenant of its leasehold interest shall be effective unless and until the applicable Leasehold Mortgagee cure period has expired without cure.

(e) **Cure by Mortgagee.** Landlord shall accept performance by a Leasehold Mortgagee as if performed by Tenant, and shall not be entitled to any fee, charge, or additional rent by reason of any such cure. Any amount expended by a Leasehold Mortgagee to cure shall be added to the secured obligations of the Leasehold Mortgage and shall bear interest as provided in the loan documents.

(f) **Access.** During any cure period, Landlord shall afford each Leasehold Mortgagee and its agents, designees, and prospective purchasers reasonable access to the Premises to inspect, complete, or manage the Improvements, and shall not obstruct any such party's efforts to cure.

### Section 10.4 New Lease.

(a) If this Lease is terminated for any reason (including Tenant's default, voluntary surrender, rejection in any bankruptcy or insolvency proceeding, operation of law, or a Reverter Termination), each Leasehold Mortgagee (or its designee) shall have the right, exercisable by written request delivered to Landlord within sixty (60) days after such Leasehold Mortgagee's receipt of notice of termination, to obtain a new ground lease of the Premises (a "**New Lease**") on the same terms and conditions as this Lease, for the remainder of the Term (including any period that would have remained had this Lease not been terminated), subject to the following:

> (i) the New Lease shall be effective as of the date of termination of this Lease, and Landlord shall execute and deliver the New Lease within thirty (30) days after the Leasehold Mortgagee's written request;
>
> (ii) the Leasehold Mortgagee (or its designee) shall cure all monetary defaults existing under this Lease within sixty (60) days after the effective date of the New Lease;
>
> (iii) the Leasehold Mortgagee (or its designee) shall cure all non-monetary defaults that are reasonably susceptible of cure within ninety (90) days after the effective date of the New Lease, or, if such cure cannot reasonably be completed within such period, shall commence cure within such period and thereafter diligently pursue cure to completion, not to exceed an additional one hundred eighty (180) days;
>
> (iv) the Leasehold Mortgagee (or its designee) shall assume all obligations under the New Lease prospectively from its effective date, and shall not be liable for any obligation or liability of Tenant arising before such date, including any obligation to pay Reverter Compensation or any Landlord Damages;
>
> (v) the New Lease shall have priority in all respects equal to the priority of this Lease, and shall not require any additional rent, fee, or increase in rent by reason of its execution;
>
> (vi) the New Lease shall demise the Premises together with all Improvements, without additional rent, and no Reverter Compensation or Landlord Damages shall be payable in connection with the New Lease;
>
> (vii) all subleases, licenses, and occupancy agreements entered into by Tenant or any subtenant before the termination shall be recognized by Landlord under the New Lease, and Landlord shall accept attornment of such subtenants; and
>
> (viii) the New Lease shall contain the provisions of this Article 10, Article 11, and Article 13, and shall otherwise be in form reasonably acceptable to the Leasehold Mortgagee.

(b) If the Leasehold Mortgagee does not exercise its right under this Section 10.4 within the sixty (60) day period, the right shall lapse as to that Leasehold Mortgagee but shall not affect the rights of any other Leasehold Mortgagee.

(c) Landlord shall, upon the request of any Leasehold Mortgagee, execute and deliver a conditional New Lease, effective upon the occurrence of the events described in Section 10.4(a), in recordable form, within thirty (30) days after such request. Such conditional New Lease shall be delivered at the time the Leasehold Mortgage is recorded and shall satisfy the requirements of any Leasehold Mortgagee.

### Section 10.5 No Surrender or Amendment Without Consent.

For so long as any Leasehold Mortgage remains in effect, Landlord shall not accept a voluntary surrender, cancellation, or termination of this Lease, and Landlord and Tenant shall not amend, modify, supplement, or terminate this Lease in any material respect, without the prior written consent of the Leasehold Mortgagee. Any purported surrender, amendment, modification, supplement, or termination effected without such consent shall be void as against the Leasehold Mortgagee, and this Lease shall continue in full force and effect as if the same had not occurred. Nothing in this Section 10.5 shall require the consent of a Leasehold Mortgagee to any amendment that (i) corrects a clerical or typographical error, (ii) does not affect the Leasehold Mortgagee's rights under this Lease, or (iii) is required by Applicable Law and does not increase Tenant's monetary obligations.

### Section 10.6 Foreclosure, Deed in Lieu, and Assignment.

(a) Each Leasehold Mortgagee shall have the unconditional right to foreclose its Leasehold Mortgage (by judicial foreclosure, power of sale, or otherwise), to accept a deed or assignment in lieu of foreclosure, and to assign this Lease to a transferee at or following any foreclosure sale or deed-in-lieu transfer, without Landlord's prior consent.

(b) Any transferee under this Section 10.6 shall meet reasonable financial and experience qualifications substantially similar to those required of Tenant as of the Effective Date. Landlord shall not unreasonably withhold, condition, or delay recognition of any such transferee as Tenant under this Lease, and shall execute and deliver such estoppels, consents, and other documents reasonably requested to confirm or effectuate the foreclosure, transfer, or assignment.

(c) No foreclosure, deed-in-lieu transfer, or assignment under this Section 10.6 shall constitute a Transfer for purposes of Article 11, shall trigger the right of first refusal under Section 11.5, or shall require the payment of any fee, transfer charge, or additional rent.

(d) Landlord shall not terminate this Lease by reason of any Transfer effected under this Section 10.6, and the transferee shall not be liable for any act, omission, or liability of Tenant arising before the date of the transfer.

### Section 10.7 Subordination, Non-Disturbance, and Attornment Agreement.

Landlord shall execute and deliver to each Leasehold Mortgagee, on or before the Lease Commencement Date (as to Bayside) and within thirty (30) days after request (as to any other Leasehold Mortgagee), a Subordination, Non-Disturbance, and Attornment Agreement substantially in the form of **Exhibit E** and reasonably acceptable to the Leasehold Mortgagee, which shall include, at a minimum: (a) Landlord's acknowledgment of the existence, amount, and priority of the Leasehold Mortgage; (b) Landlord's agreement not to disturb the Leasehold Mortgagee's security interest or the rights of any purchaser at foreclosure or transferee by deed in lieu, so long as Tenant's obligations are performed or cured by the Leasehold Mortgagee; (c) Landlord's agreement to recognize the Leasehold Mortgagee, its designee, or any such purchaser or transferee as Tenant upon the same terms; (d) the notice and cure provisions of Section 10.2 and Section 10.3; (e) the New Lease rights of Section 10.4; (f) provisions confirming that insurance and condemnation proceeds attributable to the Improvements shall be available to the Leasehold Mortgagee as its interest may appear, subject to Section 13.6; (g) a prohibition on amendment, surrender, or termination in violation of Section 10.5; and (h) such other provisions as the Leasehold Mortgagee may reasonably require. The SNDA shall be recordable and shall be recorded at Tenant's cost.

### Section 10.8 Bankruptcy and Insolvency.

If Tenant becomes a debtor in any case under Title 11 of the United States Code or any similar state insolvency proceeding:

(a) Landlord shall, within five (5) Business Days, give written notice to each Leasehold Mortgagee, and shall not object to any motion by a Leasehold Mortgagee that the trustee, debtor in possession, or other party in interest assume or reject this Lease in a timely manner consistent with 11 U.S.C. Section 365.

(b) Each Leasehold Mortgagee shall have the right to cure any default under this Lease and to provide adequate assurance of future performance on behalf of Tenant, to the extent necessary to prevent rejection of this Lease, and Landlord shall accept such performance.

(c) The New Lease rights under Section 10.4 shall survive any rejection of this Lease in bankruptcy to the fullest extent permitted by Applicable Law, and Landlord shall recognize the Leasehold Mortgagee's right to obtain a New Lease notwithstanding such rejection.

(d) This Lease shall not be deemed terminated solely by reason of the filing of a bankruptcy petition, the rejection of this Lease, or the operation of any automatic stay, and no provision of this Lease shall constitute an ipso facto default or termination provision to the extent prohibited by 11 U.S.C. Section 365(e) or (f).

### Section 10.9 Multiple Mortgagees.

If more than one Leasehold Mortgage is outstanding, Landlord may rely on the most senior Leasehold Mortgagee for all purposes of this Article 10. The Leasehold Mortgagees may, by written notice to Landlord, designate a single representative to act on their behalf, and Landlord shall deal with such representative for the purposes of Articles 10, 13, and 15.

### Section 10.10 No Merger.

No merger of the leasehold estate into the fee shall occur by reason of (a) Landlord's acquisition of the leasehold estate, (b) any Transfer, (c) any foreclosure or deed in lieu, or (d) any exercise by Landlord of the right of first refusal under Section 11.5, unless Landlord and each Leasehold Mortgagee otherwise agree in writing.

### Section 10.11 Mortgagee Not Obligated.

No Leasehold Mortgagee shall be obligated to perform any obligation of Tenant under this Lease except to the extent it becomes the tenant under a New Lease or acquires the leasehold estate and takes possession, and then only for obligations accruing from and after such date.

## ARTICLE 11. ASSIGNMENT, SUBLETTING, AND RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL

### Section 11.1 Transfers Requiring Consent.

Subject to Section 11.3, Tenant shall not effect a Transfer without Landlord's prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. Any purported Transfer in violation of this Article 11 shall be void.

### Section 11.2 Standard for Consent; Deemed Consent.

(a) Landlord may consider only (i) the financial capacity of the proposed transferee, (ii) the experience of the proposed transferee in the ownership or operation of properties similar to the Project, and (iii) whether the proposed transferee's intended use is a Permitted Use. Landlord may not withhold consent by reason of the transferee's identity as a competitor, institutional investor, or fund, or by reason of the structure of a financing.

(b) Landlord shall not charge any fee, transfer premium, or other consideration in connection with any consent, other than reimbursement of Landlord's reasonable out-of-pocket legal costs, not to exceed $7,500 per Transfer.

(c) If Landlord does not deliver a written response within twenty (20) Business Days after receipt of a complete request for consent (including the information described in Section 11.2(a)), Landlord shall be deemed to have consented.

### Section 11.3 Permitted Transfers.

The following (each, a "**Permitted Transfer**") may be made without Landlord's consent and without triggering the right of first refusal:

(a) any Transfer to an Affiliate of Tenant;

(b) any Transfer of direct or indirect interests in Tenant or in any member or partner of Tenant, including (i) the pledge of one hundred percent (100%) of the membership interests in Tenant to Bayside or any other Leasehold Mortgagee, (ii) any foreclosure of, or transfer in lieu of foreclosure of, such pledged interests, (iii) the admission or withdrawal of members, (iv) any recapitalization, and (v) any transfer of interests by reason of death, disability, divorce, or estate planning;

(c) any Transfer to a Qualified Mortgagee, and any Transfer by a Leasehold Mortgagee or its designee under Section 10.6;

(d) any Transfer by reason of merger, consolidation, conversion, or reorganization of Tenant, provided that the surviving entity assumes this Lease;

(e) any Transfer to a joint venture, partnership, or co-investment vehicle in which Tenant or an Affiliate holds an interest, and any Transfer to a real estate investment trust or an umbrella partnership real estate investment trust;

(f) any sublease of individual units or portions of the Project in the ordinary course under Section 11.4;

(g) any Transfer by operation of law, including a Transfer by devise, descent, or bankruptcy; and

(h) any Transfer to a replacement developer, general contractor, or property manager installed by a Leasehold Mortgagee under Section 7.6(c), or to any Person acquiring the leasehold estate in a transaction approved by the Leasehold Mortgagee.

### Section 11.4 Subletting.

Tenant may sublease individual residential units, office floors, and retail spaces, and may grant licenses and occupancy agreements, in the ordinary course of the operation of the Project without Landlord's consent. Any sublease of the entire Premises, or of substantially all of the Premises, to a single subtenant shall require Landlord's consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed and shall be subject to Section 11.2. No sublease shall release Tenant from its obligations under this Lease.

### Section 11.5 Right of First Refusal.

(a) During the period from the Lease Commencement Date through September 30, 2045 (the "**ROFR Period**"), if Tenant proposes to Transfer this Lease (in whole) to a Person that is not an Affiliate for consideration, Landlord shall have a right of first refusal to acquire Tenant's leasehold interest on the same terms and subject to the conditions of the proposed Transfer.

(b) Tenant shall deliver written notice (an "**Assignment Notice**") identifying the proposed transferee, the material terms (including price), and a copy of the proposed agreement or letter of intent. Landlord shall have sixty (60) days after receipt to elect to acquire the leasehold interest by written notice to Tenant.

(c) If Landlord elects, the closing shall occur within sixty (60) days after Landlord's election (or concurrently with the proposed Transfer, if later), on the terms set forth in the Assignment Notice, and Landlord shall pay all transfer taxes and recording costs. If Landlord fails to close when required, the election shall lapse and the right of first refusal shall terminate as to that proposed Transfer.

(d) If Landlord does not elect within the sixty (60) day period, Tenant may complete the proposed Transfer to the identified transferee on terms no more favorable to the transferee than those set forth in the Assignment Notice, at any time within one hundred eighty (180) days after the expiration of such period, without further offer to Landlord. If the Transfer does not close within such period or the terms become more favorable to the transferee, the right of first refusal shall be reinstated.

(e) The right of first refusal shall expire at the end of the ROFR Period and shall not apply to any Transfer occurring after September 30, 2045.

### Section 11.6 Carve-Outs from the Right of First Refusal; Recorded Declaration.

(a) The right of first refusal shall not apply to, and the term "Transfer" shall not include, any of the following: (i) the grant, amendment, renewal, replacement, enforcement, or foreclosure of any Leasehold Mortgage; (ii) any Transfer by a Leasehold Mortgagee or its designee under Section 10.6, including any assignment following foreclosure or deed in lieu; (iii) any Permitted Transfer under Section 11.3; (iv) any sublease under Section 11.4; (v) any Transfer of direct or indirect equity interests in Tenant; (vi) any involuntary Transfer; (vii) any Transfer to a replacement developer or manager installed by a Leasehold Mortgagee under Section 7.6(c); and (viii) any Transfer of the Premises or any interest therein to a Governmental Authority by reason of Condemnation.

(b) Landlord and Tenant acknowledge that a Declaration of Right of First Refusal dated September 8, 2019, recorded at Volume 405, Page 55 of the Port Calloway Land Records (the "**ROFR Declaration**"), is a matter of record and, as recorded, contains no exception for transfers resulting from foreclosure, deed in lieu of foreclosure, the exercise of remedies by a leasehold mortgagee, or assignments by a leasehold mortgagee or its designee following foreclosure. The ROFR Declaration also, by its terms, extends to any proposed assignment of "the leasehold interest in the land," which would literally encompass the grant of a Leasehold Mortgage.

(c) Landlord shall, on or before the Lease Commencement Date, execute, deliver, and record an amendment to the ROFR Declaration, in form reasonably satisfactory to Tenant, Bayside, and the title company, which (i) implements the carve-outs in Section 11.6(a), (ii) confirms that the grant, enforcement, and foreclosure of a Leasehold Mortgage does not constitute an assignment of the leasehold interest for purposes of the ROFR Declaration, (iii) confirms that the ROFR Declaration applies only during the ROFR Period, and (iv) subordinates the ROFR Declaration to this Lease and to the Leasehold Mortgages. The delivery and recording of such amendment is a condition to the Lease Commencement Date under Section 2.6(a)(ix).

(d) Landlord shall not exercise, and shall not assign, the right of first refusal in a manner that would impair the Leasehold Mortgagee's security interest, and any exercise of the right of first refusal shall be subject to Section 10.10 (no merger) and to the Leasehold Mortgagee's rights under Article 10.

### Section 11.7 Conditions to Transfers.

(a) Each Transfer (other than a Permitted Transfer of equity interests) shall be documented by a written assumption agreement under which the transferee assumes all obligations of Tenant under this Lease arising after the transfer date.

(b) For a Permitted Transfer to an Affiliate, or a Transfer to a transferee with a tangible net worth not less than Tenant's tangible net worth as of the Effective Date, Tenant shall be released from the obligations of this Lease arising after the transfer date, and Landlord shall execute a release reasonably requested by Tenant or the Leasehold Mortgagee.

(c) For any other Transfer, Tenant shall remain liable for obligations accruing before the transfer date and shall guarantee the transferee's obligations for so long as Tenant (or its successor) retains a direct or indirect interest in the transferee.

## ARTICLE 9. USE; OPERATIONS; AFFORDABLE HOUSING; OPEN SPACE; MAINTENANCE

### Section 9.1 Permitted Uses.

The Premises may be used for the following purposes and for no other purpose: (a) residential apartments for rent only (no condominium, cooperative, or for-sale units); (b) Class A office; (c) ground-floor retail, excluding adult entertainment establishments, firearms sales, pawnshops, and gasoline service stations; (d) restaurants, including those licensed for liquor service by the Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection; (e) accessory structured and below-grade parking; and (f) uses ancillary to the foregoing, including amenity space, leasing offices, management offices, and building systems.

### Section 9.2 Prohibited Uses.

No industrial, manufacturing, warehousing, or self-storage use shall be permitted. No use shall be permitted that (a) violates the ELUR, the Remediation Standard Regulations, the Affordable Housing Covenant, or any other Applicable Law; (b) constitutes a nuisance or unreasonably interferes with the use and enjoyment of neighboring property; (c) creates a material risk of fire, explosion, or release of Hazardous Materials beyond the quantities customary for the operation of a mixed-use project; or (d) would impair the insurability of the Premises or the Improvements.

### Section 9.3 Ground-Floor Uses; ELUR Restriction.

(a) Tenant shall not construct dwelling units on the ground floor of any building within the Project, and no habitable residential space shall be located at or below finished grade, in compliance with the ELUR.

(b) The ground floor of the Residential Tower may be used for retail and commercial tenancies and for non-habitable ancillary building functions, including the residential lobby, leasing office, package and mail room, building management office, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing rooms, parking, loading, bicycle storage, and resident amenity areas (including a fitness center and resident lounge).

(c) The parties acknowledge the interpretive ambiguity described in Section 5.6(b). Tenant's rights under Section 5.6(d) and Section 5.6(e) (redesign or termination) are Tenant's sole remedies for any determination by DEEP that any such ground-floor ancillary use is prohibited by the ELUR, and no such determination shall constitute a Tenant Event of Default.

(d) Affordable dwelling units shall be located exclusively on the second floor and above, in accordance with the recommendation of Halcyon Environmental Consultants Inc. in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment.

### Section 9.4 Affordable Housing.

(a) **Requirement.** Not less than fifteen percent (15%) of the residential dwelling units constructed within the Project shall be designated as affordable housing units available to households earning at or below eighty percent (80%) of Area Median Income, for the duration of the Term (the "Affordable Units"). The requirement shall not be reduced, eliminated, or relocated off the Premises, and shall be documented in a recorded declaration or regulatory agreement reasonably satisfactory to Landlord and consistent with the recorded Affordable Housing Restrictive Covenant (Volume 408, Page 230 of the Port Calloway Land Records).

(b) **Calculation.** The number of Affordable Units shall be calculated on the basis of the total number of residential dwelling units in the Project as finally designed, rounded up to the next whole unit. If the total unit count changes during the Term by reason of renovation, conversion, or partial demolition, the fifteen percent (15%) requirement shall be recalculated on the basis of the revised unit count, and Tenant shall designate or de-designate units so as to maintain at least fifteen percent (15%) Affordable Units.

(c) **Area Median Income.** Area Median Income shall be determined annually by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development for the metropolitan statistical area applicable to the City of Port Calloway. The parties acknowledge that the recorded Affordable Housing Restrictive Covenant identifies the New Haven-Milford, Connecticut Metropolitan Statistical Area, that the Term Sheet refers to the "Port Calloway Metropolitan Statistical Area," and that the ALTA/NSPS Survey narrative refers to the Bridgeport-Stamford-Norwalk HUD Metro Fair Market Rent Area. The recorded covenant governs, and, if HUD changes the applicable geographic area in which Port Calloway is located, the successor HUD area applicable to Port Calloway shall govern. The parties shall execute an amended or supplemental declaration to conform the recorded covenant to the HUD area actually applicable, at Tenant's cost, upon request of either party.

(d) **Distribution and Unit Mix.** Affordable Units shall be distributed proportionately across unit types (studio, one-bedroom, two-bedroom, and larger units) and shall not be concentrated on any single floor or in any single building segment, to the extent consistent with Applicable Law and the recorded covenant.

(e) **Marketing, Verification, and Compliance.** Tenant shall market Affordable Units in accordance with an affirmative marketing plan, verify household income at initial occupancy and annually thereafter, and deliver to Landlord an annual compliance certificate with a rent roll identifying the Affordable Units, unit sizes, rents charged, and household income bands. Tenant may engage a qualified compliance administrator, and its reasonable costs shall be an operating expense of the Project.

(f) **Enforcement.** If Landlord believes Tenant is not in compliance with this Section 9.4, Landlord shall deliver written notice specifying the alleged non-compliance, and Tenant shall have sixty (60) days to cure (or, if the non-compliance cannot reasonably be cured within sixty (60) days, to commence cure and diligently pursue it to completion). Landlord's sole remedies for non-compliance with this Section 9.4 shall be specific performance and injunctive relief. Non-compliance with this Section 9.4 shall not constitute a Tenant Event of Default, shall not give rise to any right of termination, reverter, or forfeiture, and shall not entitle Landlord to draw upon the Security Deposit.

(g) **No Reduction by Landlord.** Landlord shall not amend, modify, release, or subordinate the Affordable Housing Restrictive Covenant in any manner that would reduce the requirement, and shall not consent to any such reduction.

### Section 9.5 Public Open Space.

(a) The Project shall include not less than eight thousand (8,000) square feet of publicly accessible open space on the waterfront (eastern) side of the Premises, designed and maintained by Tenant at its sole cost, and connected to the existing public pedestrian promenade.

(b) The design and programming of the public open space shall be subject to Landlord's reasonable approval, exercised concurrently with, and within the same time period as, the City's site plan review process. If Landlord does not deliver written objections within thirty (30) days after Tenant's submission of the open space design, the design shall be deemed approved. Landlord's approval shall not be conditioned on any element that would materially increase Tenant's cost or reduce the developable area of the Premises beyond the requirements of the Approvals.

(c) The public open space shall not be dedicated to the public, shall not be conveyed to Landlord or the City, and shall remain part of the Premises and, upon the expiration or termination of this Lease, shall pass to Landlord with the Improvements without additional compensation, subject to Section 16.2.

(d) Tenant may establish reasonable rules and hours for the public open space consistent with public access and the pedestrian easement, may close the space temporarily for maintenance, emergencies, or events, and shall not be required to accept or host any event or programming proposed by Landlord or the City except as Tenant may agree.

(e) Landlord shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Tenant from and against all claims, liabilities, losses, and expenses arising from the use of the public pedestrian access easement, the waterfront promenade, and the public open space by members of the public, except to the extent caused by Tenant's negligence in the maintenance of the public open space or by a condition created by Tenant. Landlord and the City shall maintain their respective insurance covering the promenade and the easement areas, and each party waives subrogation against the other to the extent of insurance proceeds received.

### Section 9.6 Maintenance and Repair; Bulkhead.

(a) Tenant shall maintain, repair, and replace the Premises and the Improvements in good order, condition, and repair throughout the Term, reasonable wear and tear, Casualty, and Condemnation excepted, and shall keep the Premises free of liens, rubbish, and unsafe conditions.

(b) **Bulkhead.** The parties acknowledge that the approximately 480 linear feet of bulkhead along the eastern boundary is in fair to poor condition, as described in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment and the Survey, and that its rehabilitation or replacement is not included in the environmental remediation cost estimates. Tenant shall be responsible for the cost of rehabilitating or replacing the bulkhead as necessary for the construction and operation of the Project; provided, however, that Landlord shall reimburse Tenant for the portion of such cost attributable to the deteriorated condition of the bulkhead existing as of the Lease Commencement Date (as distinguished from the cost attributable to the Project's design, the required design loads, flood and coastal resilience requirements, and Tenant's improvements), as determined by an independent marine structural engineer jointly engaged by the parties within sixty (60) days after the Lease Commencement Date. If the parties cannot agree on the engineer, the engineer shall be appointed by the Expert procedure in Section 18.3(c). Landlord shall pay its share within thirty (30) days after the engineer's determination, or, at Tenant's election, Landlord's share shall be credited against Base Rent. Landlord's obligation under this Section 9.6(b) is in addition to, and not in lieu of, Landlord's obligations under Section 17.1(g) with respect to the pending mechanics' lien, and does not extend to the cost of bulkhead maintenance or replacement attributable to conditions arising after the Lease Commencement Date.

(c) Tenant shall be responsible for all maintenance, repair, and replacement of the bulkhead and all waterfront structures after the Lease Commencement Date, including compliance with any permit or condition applicable to the pedestrian easement area.

### Section 9.7 Operational Standards.

Tenant shall operate the Project in a first-class manner consistent with institutional-quality mixed-use properties in the region, shall provide customary management, security, cleaning, and life-safety services, and may engage Affiliates as manager, leasing agent, or developer without Landlord's consent, provided that any such engagement is on arm's-length terms.

### Section 9.8 Compliance with Laws; Accessibility.

Tenant shall cause the Project to comply with all Applicable Law, including the Connecticut State Building Code, the Connecticut Fire Safety Code, the accessibility provisions of the Americans with Disabilities Act and the Connecticut Fair Housing Act, floodplain management requirements, and the ELUR. Tenant shall maintain the minimum finished floor elevation required by the Approvals and Applicable Law, and the parties acknowledge that Tenant may elect to construct the ground floor at a finished floor elevation above fifteen (15) feet NAVD88 in order to address sea level rise and coastal resilience standards, including the standards described in Section 5 of the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment and Connecticut Public Act 23-167; no such election shall require Landlord's consent or constitute a breach of this Lease.

### Section 9.9 Signage.

Tenant may install building identification, retail, and directional signage consistent with the Approvals and applicable sign regulations, without Landlord's consent. Any signage that advertises Landlord or the City shall be subject to Landlord's prior written approval.

### Section 9.10 Landlord Access.

Landlord and its agents may enter the Premises for inspection, to perform its obligations, or to comply with Applicable Law, upon not less than forty-eight (48) hours' prior written notice (except in an emergency, in which case notice shall be given as soon as practicable), at reasonable times, in a manner that does not unreasonably interfere with the operation of the Project, and subject to Tenant's reasonable security and confidentiality requirements. Landlord shall treat as confidential all information regarding Tenant's operations, revenues, tenants, and financing obtained through any entry, and shall not disclose the same except as required by law or in connection with the enforcement of this Lease.

### Section 9.11 Tenant's Personal Property and Fixtures.

All Improvements shall be and remain Tenant's property during the Term (subject to the Leasehold Mortgage), and Tenant shall have the right to finance, encumber, insure, replace, alter, and (subject to Article 16) remove its Trade Fixtures and Personal Property.

## ARTICLE 10. LEASEHOLD MORTGAGE AND LENDER PROTECTIONS

### Section 10.1 Right to Encumber.

(a) Tenant may, without Landlord's consent, joinder, or approval, and without payment of any fee, charge, or other consideration to Landlord, grant one or more Leasehold Mortgages encumbering Tenant's entire leasehold interest in the Premises together with the Improvements, fixtures, and appurtenances, to any Qualified Mortgagee. No approval, consent, or other condition from Landlord shall be required for the recording, enforcement, foreclosure, or assignment of any Leasehold Mortgage.

(b) Landlord shall, upon request, execute and deliver a commercially reasonable consent to the Leasehold Mortgage, an estoppel certificate under Section 18.4, and the SNDA under Section 10.7, and shall reasonably cooperate with any Leasehold Mortgagee's due diligence, including by providing copies of this Lease, the Permitted Exceptions, and such title, survey, and environmental materials as are in Landlord's possession.

### Section 10.2 Notices to Leasehold Mortgagee.

Landlord shall deliver to each Leasehold Mortgagee, simultaneously with delivery to Tenant, a copy of every notice of default, notice of termination, Milestone Notice, notice of Landlord's exercise of the reverter right or of the right of first refusal, and any other notice materially affecting Tenant's leasehold interest, at the address designated by such Leasehold Mortgagee in writing (initially, Bayside Federal Lending Corp., 200 Atlantic Boulevard, Stamford, Connecticut 06902, Attention: Sandra Milliken, Senior Vice President, Commercial Real Estate Lending, with a copy to Bayside's counsel as designated). Failure to deliver any such notice to a Leasehold Mortgagee shall render the notice ineffective as to such Leasehold Mortgagee and shall suspend the running of Landlord's remedies until a copy is delivered.

### Section 10.3 Leasehold Mortgagee Cure Rights.

(a) **Monetary defaults.** Each Leasehold Mortgagee shall have sixty (60) days after its receipt of notice of any monetary default by Tenant to cure such default on Tenant's behalf.

(b) **Non-monetary defaults.** Each Leasehold Mortgagee shall have ninety (90) days after its receipt of notice of any non-monetary default by Tenant to cure such default, or, if such cure cannot reasonably be completed within ninety (90) days, to commence cure within such period and thereafter diligently and continuously prosecute the cure to completion, in which case the cure period shall extend for such time as is reasonably necessary, not to exceed an additional one hundred eighty (180) days.

(c) **Milestone Failures.** Each Leasehold Mortgagee shall have one hundred eighty (180) days after its receipt of a Milestone Notice to cure the Milestone Failure, by any of the means described in Section 7.6(c).

(d) **Additional, not concurrent.** The cure periods in this Section 10.3 are in addition to, and shall not run concurrently with, the cure periods afforded to Tenant under this Lease. No termination, reverter, forfeiture, or exercise of any remedy by Landlord that would divest Tenant of its leasehold interest shall be effective unless and until the applicable Leasehold Mortgagee cure period has expired without cure.

(e) **Cure by Mortgagee.** Landlord shall accept performance by a Leasehold Mortgagee as if performed by Tenant, and shall not be entitled to any fee, charge, or additional rent by reason of any such cure. Any amount expended by a Leasehold Mortgagee to cure shall be added to the secured obligations of the Leasehold Mortgage and shall bear interest as provided in the loan documents.

(f) **Access.** During any cure period, Landlord shall afford each Leasehold Mortgagee and its agents, designees, and prospective purchasers reasonable access to the Premises to inspect, complete, or manage the Improvements, and shall not obstruct any such party's efforts to cure.

### Section 10.4 New Lease.

(a) If this Lease is terminated for any reason (including Tenant's default, voluntary surrender, rejection in any bankruptcy or insolvency proceeding, operation of law, or a Reverter Termination), each Leasehold Mortgagee (or its designee) shall have the right, exercisable by written request delivered to Landlord within sixty (60) days after such Leasehold Mortgagee's receipt of notice of termination, to obtain a new ground lease of the Premises (a "**New Lease**") on the same terms and conditions as this Lease, for the remainder of the Term (including any period that would have remained had this Lease not been terminated), subject to the following:

> (i) the New Lease shall be effective as of the date of termination of this Lease, and Landlord shall execute and deliver the New Lease within thirty (30) days after the Leasehold Mortgagee's written request;
>
> (ii) the Leasehold Mortgagee (or its designee) shall cure all monetary defaults existing under this Lease within sixty (60) days after the effective date of the New Lease;
>
> (iii) the Leasehold Mortgagee (or its designee) shall cure all non-monetary defaults that are reasonably susceptible of cure within ninety (90) days after the effective date of the New Lease, or, if such cure cannot reasonably be completed within such period, shall commence cure within such period and thereafter diligently pursue cure to completion, not to exceed an additional one hundred eighty (180) days;
>
> (iv) the Leasehold Mortgagee (or its designee) shall assume all obligations under the New Lease prospectively from its effective date, and shall not be liable for any obligation or liability of Tenant arising before such date, including any obligation to pay Reverter Compensation or any Landlord Damages;
>
> (v) the New Lease shall have priority in all respects equal to the priority of this Lease, and shall not require any additional rent, fee, or increase in rent by reason of its execution;
>
> (vi) the New Lease shall demise the Premises together with all Improvements, without additional rent, and no Reverter Compensation or Landlord Damages shall be payable in connection with the New Lease;
>
> (vii) all subleases, licenses, and occupancy agreements entered into by Tenant or any subtenant before the termination shall be recognized by Landlord under the New Lease, and Landlord shall accept attornment of such subtenants; and
>
> (viii) the New Lease shall contain the provisions of this Article 10, Article 11, and Article 13, and shall otherwise be in form reasonably acceptable to the Leasehold Mortgagee.

(b) If the Leasehold Mortgagee does not exercise its right under this Section 10.4 within the sixty (60) day period, the right shall lapse as to that Leasehold Mortgagee but shall not affect the rights of any other Leasehold Mortgagee.

(c) Landlord shall, upon the request of any Leasehold Mortgagee, execute and deliver a conditional New Lease, effective upon the occurrence of the events described in Section 10.4(a), in recordable form, within thirty (30) days after such request. Such conditional New Lease shall be delivered at the time the Leasehold Mortgage is recorded and shall satisfy the requirements of any Leasehold Mortgagee.

### Section 10.5 No Surrender or Amendment Without Consent.

For so long as any Leasehold Mortgage remains in effect, Landlord shall not accept a voluntary surrender, cancellation, or termination of this Lease, and Landlord and Tenant shall not amend, modify, supplement, or terminate this Lease in any material respect, without the prior written consent of the Leasehold Mortgagee. Any purported surrender, amendment, modification, supplement, or termination effected without such consent shall be void as against the Leasehold Mortgagee, and this Lease shall continue in full force and effect as if the same had not occurred. Nothing in this Section 10.5 shall require the consent of a Leasehold Mortgagee to any amendment that (i) corrects a clerical or typographical error, (ii) does not affect the Leasehold Mortgagee's rights under this Lease, or (iii) is required by Applicable Law and does not increase Tenant's monetary obligations.

### Section 10.6 Foreclosure, Deed in Lieu, and Assignment.

(a) Each Leasehold Mortgagee shall have the unconditional right to foreclose its Leasehold Mortgage (by judicial foreclosure, power of sale, or otherwise), to accept a deed or assignment in lieu of foreclosure, and to assign this Lease to a transferee at or following any foreclosure sale or deed-in-lieu transfer, without Landlord's prior consent.

(b) Any transferee under this Section 10.6 shall meet reasonable financial and experience qualifications substantially similar to those required of Tenant as of the Effective Date. Landlord shall not unreasonably withhold, condition, or delay recognition of any such transferee as Tenant under this Lease, and shall execute and deliver such estoppels, consents, and other documents reasonably requested to confirm or effectuate the foreclosure, transfer, or assignment.

(c) No foreclosure, deed-in-lieu transfer, or assignment under this Section 10.6 shall constitute a Transfer for purposes of Article 11, shall trigger the right of first refusal under Section 11.5, or shall require the payment of any fee, transfer charge, or additional rent.

(d) Landlord shall not terminate this Lease by reason of any Transfer effected under this Section 10.6, and the transferee shall not be liable for any act, omission, or liability of Tenant arising before the date of the transfer.

### Section 10.7 Subordination, Non-Disturbance, and Attornment Agreement.

Landlord shall execute and deliver to each Leasehold Mortgagee, on or before the Lease Commencement Date (as to Bayside) and within thirty (30) days after request (as to any other Leasehold Mortgagee), a Subordination, Non-Disturbance, and Attornment Agreement substantially in the form of **Exhibit E** and reasonably acceptable to the Leasehold Mortgagee, which shall include, at a minimum: (a) Landlord's acknowledgment of the existence, amount, and priority of the Leasehold Mortgage; (b) Landlord's agreement not to disturb the Leasehold Mortgagee's security interest or the rights of any purchaser at foreclosure or transferee by deed in lieu, so long as Tenant's obligations are performed or cured by the Leasehold Mortgagee; (c) Landlord's agreement to recognize the Leasehold Mortgagee, its designee, or any such purchaser or transferee as Tenant upon the same terms; (d) the notice and cure provisions of Section 10.2 and Section 10.3; (e) the New Lease rights of Section 10.4; (f) provisions confirming that insurance and condemnation proceeds attributable to the Improvements shall be available to the Leasehold Mortgagee as its interest may appear, subject to Section 13.6; (g) a prohibition on amendment, surrender, or termination in violation of Section 10.5; and (h) such other provisions as the Leasehold Mortgagee may reasonably require. The SNDA shall be recordable and shall be recorded at Tenant's cost.

### Section 10.8 Bankruptcy and Insolvency.

If Tenant becomes a debtor in any case under Title 11 of the United States Code or any similar state insolvency proceeding:

(a) Landlord shall, within five (5) Business Days, give written notice to each Leasehold Mortgagee, and shall not object to any motion by a Leasehold Mortgagee that the trustee, debtor in possession, or other party in interest assume or reject this Lease in a timely manner consistent with 11 U.S.C. Section 365.

(b) Each Leasehold Mortgagee shall have the right to cure any default under this Lease and to provide adequate assurance of future performance on behalf of Tenant, to the extent necessary to prevent rejection of this Lease, and Landlord shall accept such performance.

(c) The New Lease rights under Section 10.4 shall survive any rejection of this Lease in bankruptcy to the fullest extent permitted by Applicable Law, and Landlord shall recognize the Leasehold Mortgagee's right to obtain a New Lease notwithstanding such rejection.

(d) This Lease shall not be deemed terminated solely by reason of the filing of a bankruptcy petition, the rejection of this Lease, or the operation of any automatic stay, and no provision of this Lease shall constitute an ipso facto default or termination provision to the extent prohibited by 11 U.S.C. Section 365(e) or (f).

### Section 10.9 Multiple Mortgagees.

If more than one Leasehold Mortgage is outstanding, Landlord may rely on the most senior Leasehold Mortgagee for all purposes of this Article 10. The Leasehold Mortgagees may, by written notice to Landlord, designate a single representative to act on their behalf, and Landlord shall deal with such representative for the purposes of Articles 10, 13, and 15.

### Section 10.10 No Merger.

No merger of the leasehold estate into the fee shall occur by reason of (a) Landlord's acquisition of the leasehold estate, (b) any Transfer, (c) any foreclosure or deed in lieu, or (d) any exercise by Landlord of the right of first refusal under Section 11.5, unless Landlord and each Leasehold Mortgagee otherwise agree in writing.

### Section 10.11 Mortgagee Not Obligated.

No Leasehold Mortgagee shall be obligated to perform any obligation of Tenant under this Lease except to the extent it becomes the tenant under a New Lease or acquires the leasehold estate and takes possession, and then only for obligations accruing from and after such date.

## ARTICLE 11. ASSIGNMENT, SUBLETTING, AND RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL

### Section 11.1 Transfers Requiring Consent.

Subject to Section 11.3, Tenant shall not effect a Transfer without Landlord's prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. Any purported Transfer in violation of this Article 11 shall be void.

### Section 11.2 Standard for Consent; Deemed Consent.

(a) Landlord may consider only (i) the financial capacity of the proposed transferee, (ii) the experience of the proposed transferee in the ownership or operation of properties similar to the Project, and (iii) whether the proposed transferee's intended use is a Permitted Use. Landlord may not withhold consent by reason of the transferee's identity as a competitor, institutional investor, or fund, or by reason of the structure of a financing.

(b) Landlord shall not charge any fee, transfer premium, or other consideration in connection with any consent, other than reimbursement of Landlord's reasonable out-of-pocket legal costs, not to exceed $7,500 per Transfer.

(c) If Landlord does not deliver a written response within twenty (20) Business Days after receipt of a complete request for consent (including the information described in Section 11.2(a)), Landlord shall be deemed to have consented.

### Section 11.3 Permitted Transfers.

The following (each, a "**Permitted Transfer**") may be made without Landlord's consent and without triggering the right of first refusal:

(a) any Transfer to an Affiliate of Tenant;

(b) any Transfer of direct or indirect interests in Tenant or in any member or partner of Tenant, including (i) the pledge of one hundred percent (100%) of the membership interests in Tenant to Bayside or any other Leasehold Mortgagee, (ii) any foreclosure of, or transfer in lieu of foreclosure of, such pledged interests, (iii) the admission or withdrawal of members, (iv) any recapitalization, and (v) any transfer of interests by reason of death, disability, divorce, or estate planning;

(c) any Transfer to a Qualified Mortgagee, and any Transfer by a Leasehold Mortgagee or its designee under Section 10.6;

(d) any Transfer by reason of merger, consolidation, conversion, or reorganization of Tenant, provided that the surviving entity assumes this Lease;

(e) any Transfer to a joint venture, partnership, or co-investment vehicle in which Tenant or an Affiliate holds an interest, and any Transfer to a real estate investment trust or an umbrella partnership real estate investment trust;

(f) any sublease of individual units or portions of the Project in the ordinary course under Section 11.4;

(g) any Transfer by operation of law, including a Transfer by devise, descent, or bankruptcy; and

(h) any Transfer to a replacement developer, general contractor, or property manager installed by a Leasehold Mortgagee under Section 7.6(c), or to any Person acquiring the leasehold estate in a transaction approved by the Leasehold Mortgagee.

### Section 11.4 Subletting.

Tenant may sublease individual residential units, office floors, and retail spaces, and may grant licenses and occupancy agreements, in the ordinary course of the operation of the Project without Landlord's consent. Any sublease of the entire Premises, or of substantially all of the Premises, to a single subtenant shall require Landlord's consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed and shall be subject to Section 11.2. No sublease shall release Tenant from its obligations under this Lease.

### Section 11.5 Right of First Refusal.

(a) During the period from the Lease Commencement Date through September 30, 2045 (the "**ROFR Period**"), if Tenant proposes to Transfer this Lease (in whole) to a Person that is not an Affiliate for consideration, Landlord shall have a right of first refusal to acquire Tenant's leasehold interest on the same terms and subject to the conditions of the proposed Transfer.

(b) Tenant shall deliver written notice (an "**Assignment Notice**") identifying the proposed transferee, the material terms (including price), and a copy of the proposed agreement or letter of intent. Landlord shall have sixty (60) days after receipt to elect to acquire the leasehold interest by written notice to Tenant.

(c) If Landlord elects, the closing shall occur within sixty (60) days after Landlord's election (or concurrently with the proposed Transfer, if later), on the terms set forth in the Assignment Notice, and Landlord shall pay all transfer taxes and recording costs. If Landlord fails to close when required, the election shall lapse and the right of first refusal shall terminate as to that proposed Transfer.

(d) If Landlord does not elect within the sixty (60) day period, Tenant may complete the proposed Transfer to the identified transferee on terms no more favorable to the transferee than those set forth in the Assignment Notice, at any time within one hundred eighty (180) days after the expiration of such period, without further offer to Landlord. If the Transfer does not close within such period or the terms become more favorable to the transferee, the right of first refusal shall be reinstated.

(e) The right of first refusal shall expire at the end of the ROFR Period and shall not apply to any Transfer occurring after September 30, 2045.

### Section 11.6 Carve-Outs from the Right of First Refusal; Recorded Declaration.

(a) The right of first refusal shall not apply to, and the term "Transfer" shall not include, any of the following: (i) the grant, amendment, renewal, replacement, enforcement, or foreclosure of any Leasehold Mortgage; (ii) any Transfer by a Leasehold Mortgagee or its designee under Section 10.6, including any assignment following foreclosure or deed in lieu; (iii) any Permitted Transfer under Section 11.3; (iv) any sublease under Section 11.4; (v) any Transfer of direct or indirect equity interests in Tenant; (vi) any involuntary Transfer; (vii) any Transfer to a replacement developer or manager installed by a Leasehold Mortgagee under Section 7.6(c); and (viii) any Transfer of the Premises or any interest therein to a Governmental Authority by reason of Condemnation.

(b) Landlord and Tenant acknowledge that a Declaration of Right of First Refusal dated September 8, 2019, recorded at Volume 405, Page 55 of the Port Calloway Land Records (the "**ROFR Declaration**"), is a matter of record and, as recorded, contains no exception for transfers resulting from foreclosure, deed in lieu of foreclosure, the exercise of remedies by a leasehold mortgagee, or assignments by a leasehold mortgagee or its designee following foreclosure. The ROFR Declaration also, by its terms, extends to any proposed assignment of "the leasehold interest in the land," which would literally encompass the grant of a Leasehold Mortgage.

(c) Landlord shall, on or before the Lease Commencement Date, execute, deliver, and record an amendment to the ROFR Declaration, in form reasonably satisfactory to Tenant, Bayside, and the title company, which (i) implements the carve-outs in Section 11.6(a), (ii) confirms that the grant, enforcement, and foreclosure of a Leasehold Mortgage does not constitute an assignment of the leasehold interest for purposes of the ROFR Declaration, (iii) confirms that the ROFR Declaration applies only during the ROFR Period, and (iv) subordinates the ROFR Declaration to this Lease and to the Leasehold Mortgages. The delivery and recording of such amendment is a condition to the Lease Commencement Date under Section 2.6(a)(ix).

(d) Landlord shall not exercise, and shall not assign, the right of first refusal in a manner that would impair the Leasehold Mortgagee's security interest, and any exercise of the right of first refusal shall be subject to Section 10.10 (no merger) and to the Leasehold Mortgagee's rights under Article 10.

### Section 11.7 Conditions to Transfers.

(a) Each Transfer (other than a Permitted Transfer of equity interests) shall be documented by a written assumption agreement under which the transferee assumes all obligations of Tenant under this Lease arising after the transfer date.

(b) For a Permitted Transfer to an Affiliate, or a Transfer to a transferee with a tangible net worth not less than Tenant's tangible net worth as of the Effective Date, Tenant shall be released from the obligations of this Lease arising after the transfer date, and Landlord shall execute a release reasonably requested by Tenant or the Leasehold Mortgagee.

(c) For any other Transfer, Tenant shall remain liable for obligations accruing before the transfer date and shall guarantee the transferee's obligations for so long as Tenant (or its successor) retains a direct or indirect interest in the transferee.
